# UE5MCP Implemented Features

Descriptions of implemented work, moved from IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md on 2026-10-30.
Sections marked "(unverified)" are implemented in source but not yet built/tested;
see UNTESTED_FEATURES.md. Outstanding work lives in IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md.
Historical "remaining"/"missing" notes below are preserved as written and may be stale;
IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md is the authoritative list of what is still to do.


## Status

This document tracks the UE 5.7 editor-control expansion. Existing routes remain
backward compatible. New mutations are explicit, use editor transactions where
available, mark packages dirty only after success, and save only when requested.

### Implementation priority update

Implement remaining features first; defer testing. New unverified work is tracked
in [UNTESTED_FEATURES.md](UNTESTED_FEATURES.md). That file explicitly distinguishes
implementation from prior verified milestones and lists later build/runtime/REST/
persistence checks. The full original scope remains active.

## Delivery phases

1. Shared asset capability, validation, dry-run, dirty-state, and batch operation responses.
2. Physics Asset bodies, shapes, constraints, collision pairs, refresh, and validation.
3. Texture settings and platform settings; Material and Material Instance settings and parameters.
4. Animation Sequence settings, tracks, curves, attributes, notifies, sync markers, compression, and validation.
5. Animation Blueprint graphs, variables, compilation, layout, and skeleton compatibility.
6. Blend Space axes, samples, triangulation, preview inputs, and validation.
7. Control Rig hierarchy and RigVM graph structure using public hierarchy/controller APIs.
8. Modular Rig modules, connectors, connections, overrides, compilation, and validation.
9. Documentation, Python wrappers, integration fixtures, and UE 5.7 build verification.

10. World/scene control and uncovered asset families: level loading/saving,
    world settings, sublevels, actor editing, AI assets, Data Assets, audio,
    and remaining texture workflows.

## Common API contract

Use `asset_path`, `asset_class`, `operation`, `dry_run`, `save`, `transaction`,
`warnings`, `errors`, `changed`, `dirty`, `saved`, and `validation` consistently.
Asset paths are Unreal object paths such as `/Game/Folder/Asset.Asset`.

Add `/assets/capabilities`, `/assets/validate`, `/assets/batch`,
`/assets/preview-operation`, `/assets/dirty-state`, and
`/assets/save-all-selected`. Batch responses must preserve request order and
return one result per operation. `/assets/batch` now accepts an ordered
`Operations` array while retaining the legacy single-operation request body.
It executes non-atomically, reports each success, failure, or skipped entry,
and can stop after the first error. Property values are preflighted on a
transient duplicate before each mutation; nested object-reference traversal
is rejected in the batch path until it can be validated without affecting
another UObject.
`/assets/validate` now checks the requested asset/class and, when properties
are supplied, preflights paths and values on a transient duplicate. It
reports per-field errors and the validation scope without changing or dirtying
the source asset. A live test covered valid and invalid properties, class/path
errors, and source dirty-state preservation.
`/assets/preview-operation` now preflights `set_properties` on a transient
duplicate, compares each proposed edit with the probe's prior value, and
reports per-field changes and errors. It also previews whether `save` would
act on a dirty package. A live test verified changed/unchanged and invalid
inputs while preserving the source property and dirty state.

## Asset families

### Physics Asset

Add inspect, body, shape, constraint, collision-pair, refresh, and validation
routes under `/physics-assets`. Support bone association, primitive geometry,
mass contribution, collision flags, linear/angular limits and drives,
projection, profiles, and dependency-aware deletion. Body or constraint
deletion must report affected references and require explicit confirmation.

Status: initial typed routes now inspect bodies, shapes, constraints, and
disabled collision pairs; add/delete bodies and primitive spheres, boxes, and
capsules; add/edit/delete constraints with linear/angular limits and
projection; toggle collision pairs; refresh and validate assets. Body deletion
previews attached constraint names and disabled collision pairs, requires
confirmation, and uses the public PhysicsUtilities cleanup helper. Linear and
angular drive routes now edit enable flags, strengths, modes, and targets with
transient dry-run previews. Constraint profile routes list coverage and add,
duplicate, rename, capture current constraint settings, and delete with
confirmation. Disposable-copy live tests passed drive and profile editing,
save, and cleanup. Physical Animation body-profile routes now list coverage,
add/duplicate/rename/delete profiles, and edit per-body strengths and force
limits. Typed body settings cover physics type, collision mode, mass scale,
bounds inclusion, gravity, CCD, and animation scale handling with transient
preflight. Disposable-copy live tests passed both new route families. Convex
shapes now accept 4-64 distinct local-space vertices, reject degenerate
hulls, preflight a transient Chaos cook, and expose vertices on inspection.
A disposable-copy live test passed convex shape and initial convex body
creation, save, and cleanup. `PATCH /physics-assets/shapes` now replaces an
existing convex hull's local-space vertices after geometric and transient
Chaos validation, preserving its transform and collision/mass flags. A live
test passed invalid-topology rejection, dry-run, replacement/readback, and
cleanup. Read-only validation now checks shape dimensions
and finite vertices, body mass scales and Physical Animation data, constraint
names/bones/limits/drives, profile-name coverage, and disabled collision-pair
indices. A live test detected an invalid mass scale on a duplicate while the
source asset remained valid. `GET /physics-assets/validate?include_runtime_cook=true`
now duplicates each body setup, creates its physics meshes, and reports per-body
mesh creation plus cooked convex counts; failures are returned as validation
errors. Live tests passed primitive-body and convex-body checks. Full
`GET /physics-assets/validate?include_runtime_state=true` now creates a
non-simulating transient physics preview scene, checks that every body and
constraint instance initializes, and reports per-instance results. The check
is skipped when structural errors exist; disposable-asset tests passed both
valid initialization and safe skip after an invalid mass scale. The
`include_simulation_step=true` mode advances one frame by default; callers may
request 1-600 frames with `simulation_steps`. The opt-in
`include_stability_test=true` mode defaults to 600 frames and checks every
body transform and linear/angular velocity plus every constraint at each frame.
It reports per-body and aggregate peak linear speed, angular speed, and
displacement from the starting pose, and marks the run ready only when sampled
states remain valid and finite. Optional `simulation_impulse_x/y/z` values
apply a velocity-change impulse to a transient root body and report its
displacement. A disposable Mannequin Physics Asset passed a one-frame state
check and a 30-frame impulse response; a separate convex-asset test passed
runtime body and constraint initialization. The same Mannequin fixture passed
the default 600-frame stability run, including 600 samples per body and
constraint and finite peak metrics. A live test against a disposable copy of
`PA_Mannequin` passed, including dependent constraint cleanup. A second test
saved a new body and constraint, restarted the editor, verified both, and
deleted the duplicate.

### Texture

Add inspect, settings, platform-settings, rebuild, refresh, and validation
routes under `/textures`. Support compression, LOD group, mip behavior,
address/filter, sRGB, virtual texturing, alpha coverage, streaming, mip bias,
and platform overrides. Source-file import/reimport is a separate future
capability and is not implemented by property editing.

### Material and Material Instance

Extend `/materials` and add `/material-instances` routes for inspect, settings,
parameters, compile, parent assignment, reset/clear, and validation. Support
domain, blend mode, shading model, two-sided state, usage flags, parameter
groups, static switches, scalar/vector/texture/font/runtime-VT parameters,
parent compatibility, and missing/overridden parameter reporting.

Current progress: `/material-instances/parameters` lists effective values,
groups, and local override flags for scalar, vector, texture, static switch,
font, and runtime virtual texture parameters. Typed edits cover those types;
`/material-instances/parent` checks inheritance cycles, and
`/material-instances/reset` clears dynamic and static overrides. Validation
reports a missing parent and orphaned local overrides. Broader Material
settings and deeper compatibility checks remain.

Parent Material progress: `/materials/summary` exposes domain, blend mode,
shading models, two-sided state, and active usage flags. `/materials/parameters`
lists parameter types, groups, descriptions, and defaults. The typed
`/materials/core-settings` route edits the core fields with validation and
dry-run support. `/materials/validate` now reports shader resource status and
compile errors when available; headless NullRHI reports `unavailable`.

Source-only continuation adds guarded material/function expression metadata,
material group ordering, scalar/vector/static/font defaults, scalar UI/enum refs,
instance enumeration slots/fallback, primitive-data bindings/channel labels and
texture-sample/object references/policies. Dedicated Material Parameter Collection
adapters now cover discovery/native factory creation/typed defaults/parameter
add-rename-delete/structure diagnostics, collection expression GUID references,
and current Editor/PIE world native effective values/overrides/reset. All new
adapters remain uncompiled/runtime/undo/persistence/render-output unverified;
UNTESTED_FEATURES.md tracks deferred checks. Native callbacks may compile or
reconstruct pins; world instance controls have no editor transaction/undo and
native instance access can initialize world/render state. Complete unloaded
name-based dependency analysis and broad shader/graph compatibility remain open.

### Animation Sequence

Add `/animation-sequences` routes for inspect, tracks, settings, curves,
notifies, sync markers, attributes, compression, and validation. Reuse
`AnimationBlueprintLibrary` where possible; isolate lower-level sequence edits
behind an adapter. Validate skeleton compatibility and preserve reload safety.

Current progress: `/animation-sequences/inspect`, `/tracks`, and `/timeline`
report source frame rate and keys, Skeleton bone-track matches, compression
assets, notify tracks/events, sync markers, curves, and animated attributes.
Validation checks the data model, Skeleton bones, attribute identifiers, and
notify/marker ranges and tracks. Timed notify/curve/marker requests reject
times outside the sequence, and sync-marker additions now report a rejected
editor operation. Typed `/animation-sequences/compression` edits bone/curve
compression assets, frame stripping, and error scale with dry-run and save.
Live tests covered a valid imported sequence, a malformed marker on a
disposable copy, compression edits, and saved compression state after editor
restart. Broader source-track and animation-specific settings work remains.

Attribute progress: the data-controller-backed
`/animation-sequences/attributes` route lists typed keys and supports
creation, key upsert/removal, and attribute removal for built-in float,
integer, string, and vector types. It checks the Skeleton bone, type, and key
time before mutation, and supports dry-run and save. Live tests covered all
four types, invalid bones, validation, removal, and saved float-key state
after editor restart. The route now also accepts transform text and registered
ScriptStruct paths through UE's native struct import; transform and registered
quaternion keys survived editor restart on a disposable sequence.

Bone-track progress: `/animation-sequences/bone-track-keys` pages source
transforms, while `/animation-sequences/bone-tracks` adds missing Skeleton
tracks initialized from the reference pose, removes tracks, and replaces one
source frame's transform through the animation data controller. Requests
check Skeleton membership, frame bounds, finite values, and source key count;
they support dry-run and explicit save. A disposable imported sequence passed
key edit, no-op, remove/re-add, and validation tests. A saved key survived
editor restart. The adapter expands constant raw component keys on legacy data
models and evaluates frame transforms on Sequencer-backed data models. Track
inspection identifies the storage type, and validation checks raw component
key counts without treating Sequencer storage as missing raw data.

Timing progress: `/animation-sequences/timing` changes compatible source
frame rates with bone-track resampling, or extends/trims source frames with
explicit confirmation before trimming. It preflights duration, notify bounds,
key counts, and an upper key budget. Live tests covered 30-to-60 fps and back,
pose preservation, extension, confirmed trim, validation, and saved frame-rate
state after editor restart. Bulk track replacement remains.

### Animation Blueprint

Add `/animation-blueprints` routes for inspect, graphs, variables, compile,
layout, and validation. Reuse Blueprint graph DTOs and add animation-specific
asset, state-machine, transition, pose-link, and blend metadata.

Current progress: `/animation-blueprints/inspect`, `/graphs`, `/variables`,
and `/state-machines` report the target Skeleton, nested graphs, node/pin
links, pose pins, variables, state entry targets, transition endpoints, rule
graphs, priorities, and blend settings. Graph layout resolves a full nested
graph path. Transition edits address a GUID and validate duration, priority,
and blend mode; pose-link edits use the graph schema and require explicit
confirmation before replacing another link. Compile reports status, and
validation checks the Skeleton, graph/node IDs and links, state-machine entry,
state graphs, and transition endpoints. Disposable Blueprint tests passed
top-level and nested layout, transition edits, pose-link disconnect/reconnect
and replacement, compile, and validation. A saved transition blend edit
survived editor restart. `/animation-blueprints/state-machines` now creates
states and transitions with their native bound graphs, reassigns entry,
renames states, edits reset-on-entry, and removes states/transitions with
confirmation and entry-target protection. Live lifecycle tests and a
two-session saved state/transition test passed. Conduits, aliases, custom
transition graphs, and more complete animation-node authoring remain.

### Blend Space

Add `/blend-spaces` routes for inspect, axes, samples, triangulation rebuild,
and validation. Use stable sample identifiers, validate duplicate/out-of-range
coordinates, and support both `UBlendSpace` and `UBlendSpace1D`.

Status: sample add, animation replacement by index or unique coordinate,
coordinate move, and confirmed deletion use current public APIs. Requests
preflight skeleton compatibility and duplicate/out-of-range coordinates,
support dry-run and explicit save, and modify within an editor transaction.
Axis listing and property editing support range, grid, snapping, wrapping, and
display name with sample-range preflight. Rebuild uses `ResampleData`, and
preview reports the effective input and weighted animation samples. Live tests
on disposable Blend Space copies passed sample edits, axis edits, preview,
rebuild, save, and cleanup. A dedicated `UBlendSpace1D` fixture test passed
axis bounds, unused-coordinate rejection, interpolation, segment rebuild,
save, and cleanup. Sample listings include persistent IDs; edits can select by
ID or index. IDs survive plugin edits that shift indices or snap coordinates.
A two-session test verified IDs after deletion, grid editing, save, and reload.
Changes made by unrelated tools can make an ID unresolvable when they replace
its sample without preserving the plugin's identity metadata. The read-only
validation route now reports axis, Skeleton, sample animation/coordinate,
overlap, rate-scale, and interpolation-data errors. A live 1D fixture test
verified both an empty-asset error and a valid populated result; the existing
2D Blend Space also validated without errors.

### Control Rig and Modular Rig

Add `/control-rigs` for hierarchy and RigVM graph inspection/editing, compile,
layout, and validation. Support bones, controls, nulls, curves, spaces,
sockets, connectors, transforms, limits, node creation/deletion, pin defaults,
links, and positions. Add `/modular-rigs` for module references, namespaces,
parenting, connectors, connections, overrides, recompilation, and unresolved
connector reporting. Mutations must use public controller APIs rather than
direct internal-array edits.

Status: typed Control Rig hierarchy listing and add/rename/confirmed-delete
operations now use the public `URigHierarchyController` through UE 5.7's
Control Rig asset interface. Add supports nulls, user bones, curves, controls,
and sockets, with optional parent and initial transform for transform
elements. Control values support float, scale-float, bool, integer, Vector2D,
position, scale, rotator, transform, transform-without-scale, and Euler
transform representations. Integer controls can bind to a loaded UEnum, accept
member names on writes, reject sentinels, and report both member names and
numeric values. Controls expose initial/current typed values and their primary
axis. Limits support scalar and per-dimension vector/transform
types, with selected dimensions and minimum/maximum bounds. Enum-backed
integer controls have tested member-name writes, member and numeric readback,
and sentinels are rejected. Typed settings also edit display names, validated
shape names, linear shape colors, visibility policy, the visible flag, shape
transforms, limit display, parent grouping, and preferred Euler rotation order.
Animation roles include controls, channels, proxy controls, and visual cues;
proxy targets must name other controls and cannot introduce a cycle.
The disposable hierarchy fixture passed shape and animation-setting edits,
shape-value readback, a two-target proxy, rotation order, and indirect
proxy-cycle rejection, then compiled and removed its copy.
Dry-run deletion reports descendant count. RigVM graph inspection lists model
nodes, pin defaults and constant state, positions, and links; a compile route
reports VM errors and warnings. `POST /control-rigs/validate` checks graph, node,
pin, link, orphaned-pin, unresolved-template, and contained-graph structure,
with optional VM compilation. RigVM controller routes now add/remove unit and branch nodes,
add comment, constant, make/break struct, If, Select, enum, and typed array
nodes, create function-local variables and getter/setter nodes, edit positions

Replacing incoming links on occupied pins requires confirmation. Function
library routes create mutable or pure definitions and preview/reference-check

`GET /control-rigs/templates` lists registered
RigVM template notations and their supported unit structs; graph edits can add

Disposable rig copies passed branch-pin checks, valid/invalid invoke-entry
creation, target-event and pin readback, compatible/incompatible injected-unit

restoration, comment and constant readback,
FVector make/break creation, typed If/Select creation, enum default readback,
array Add pin/type checks, local variable add/default/rename/getter/setter/

## World, Level, Scene, and Spawn/Edit Coverage Audit

The current implementation has live editor-world control, but it is not a
complete world or scene editor. The existing `/editor/status` route reports the
current editor world/map and play state, while `/worlds/load` performs a guarded
map transition that validates the target, rejects PIE, and requires explicit
confirmation when dirty packages exist. The `/editor/actors` routes support
listing/searching, spawning, selecting, duplicating, and confirmed deletion.
Viewport camera get/set is also implemented. These operations target the
currently open editor world only.

The following capabilities are still missing and must be added as dedicated
editor routes rather than relying only on generic reflected property editing:

- World and level asset inspection, creation, load/open, save, rename, and
  validation for `UWorld` and `ULevel` assets.
- Additional map load modes (such as template loading) and save-before-load
  behavior beyond the existing confirmed discard workflow.
- World settings editing, world composition or World Partition inspection,
  data-layer control, level-instance control, and sublevel add/remove/visibility
  operations.
- Actor editing after spawn: transform, label, folder, mobility, visibility,
  property paths, attachment, components, and level ownership. Spawn should
  return a stable actor path and support optional template/asset, collision,
  deferred construction, and transaction information.
- Scene organization: actor folders, layers, data layers, selection sets,
  level snapshots, and deterministic actor queries.
- Landscape, foliage, spline, volume, reflection-capture, light, and
  post-process scene-object authoring where public editor APIs are available.
- Level Sequence and cinematic asset inspection/editing, including bindings,
  tracks, sections, keys, playback settings, and possessable/spawnable actors.

Proposed route families:

- `/worlds/inspect`, `/worlds/settings`, `/worlds/load`, `/worlds/save`,
  `/worlds/validate`, `/worlds/partition`, `/worlds/data-layers`.
- `/levels/inspect`, `/levels/sublevels`, `/levels/sublevels/add`,
  `/levels/sublevels/remove`, `/levels/visibility`, `/levels/validate`.
- `/scene/actors/inspect`, `/scene/actors/spawn`, `/scene/actors/properties`,
  `/scene/actors/transform`, `/scene/actors/attach`, `/scene/actors/folders`,
  `/scene/actors/delete`.
- `/level-sequences/inspect`, `/level-sequences/bindings`,
  `/level-sequences/tracks`, `/level-sequences/sections`,
  `/level-sequences/keys`, `/level-sequences/validate`.

All world/level mutations must require explicit save and confirmation for
destructive operations, preserve the current world when validation fails, and
report unsaved packages, affected levels, actor references, and transaction
state.

## Cinematic and Sequencer Asset Coverage Audit

Initial cinematic routes are now implemented for Level Sequence assets. The
adapter exposes Movie Scene timing, playback bounds, binding metadata, master
and object-bound track/section metadata, section frame ranges and channel
counts, settings mutation through reflected Movie Scene properties, creation,
and basic validation. Initial transform, visibility, float-property, fade,
audio, and skeletal-animation track/section authoring and selected channel
key editing are implemented; specialized cinematic tracks remain planned.

Source-only continuation adds typed Float/Double/Bool/Byte/Integer/Object/Event
channel discovery, native full channel snapshot guards, fallback defaults where
supported, numeric extrapolation/interpolation/manual tangents/weights, and
numeric/discrete/object key CRUD/time movement. Native event-trigger key insertion,
move/delete/duplicate, director endpoint discovery/creation/binding and scalar
payload editing use public editor helpers and guarded director compilation.
Generic track creation now accepts `event` for master or object-bound scope;
native trigger/repeater sections, endpoint parameter add/remove, repeater payloads,
raw typed channel sampling, key duplication/offsets and integer interpolation policy
are implemented in source. Section blend/completion modes, manual easing durations,
built-in/external curve functions and native automatic easing recalculation now have
typed guarded adapters. Broader endpoint body authoring and complete runtime/cook/graph
compatibility remain open. All new adapters are uncompiled/runtime/undo/persistence unverified;
no continuation builds/tests/native execution have run. See UNTESTED_FEATURES.md.

Add dedicated support for:

- Level Sequence inspection, creation, duplication, settings, playback range,
  display rate, tick resolution, evaluation settings, and validation.
- Movie Scene bindings for possessable and spawnable actors, object binding
  IDs, spawnable templates, binding names, and binding removal/repair.
- Track and section authoring for transform, visibility, property, material,
  skeletal animation, audio, camera cut, event, fade, cinematic shot, and
  sub-sequence tracks.
- Key editing for scalar, vector, transform, color, bool, enum, object, and
  event channels, including interpolation, tangents, extrapolation, and
  section ranges.
- Camera actors, camera cuts, shot ordering, focal settings, lens settings,
  focus settings, and deterministic cinematic layout.
- Sub-sequence nesting, sequence hierarchy inspection, playback validation,
  missing-binding detection, and cyclic-reference protection.
- Take Recorder and cinematic metadata only where public UE 5.7 editor APIs
  are available; raw source media recording is outside the first release.

Proposed route families:

- `/level-sequences/inspect`, `/level-sequences/create`,
  `/level-sequences/settings`, `/level-sequences/bindings`,
  `/level-sequences/spawnables`, `/level-sequences/subsequences`.
- `/level-sequences/tracks`, `/level-sequences/sections`,
  `/level-sequences/keys`, `/level-sequences/layout`, `/level-sequences/compile`,
  `/level-sequences/validate`.
- `/cinematic/cameras`, `/cinematic/camera-cuts`, `/cinematic/shots`,
  `/cinematic/takes`, and `/cinematic/validate`.

Use `LevelSequenceEditor`, `MovieScene`, and public Sequencer/channel APIs
where available. Keep version-specific editor code behind an adapter and
report unsupported track/channel types instead of silently mutating them.

## AI Asset Coverage Audit

Initial native Behavior Tree graph authoring and typed Blackboard authoring
and native compound decorator expressions are implemented. Specialized Behavior
Tree nodes/providers, broader StateTree parameter/binding/linked-tree coverage and AI Perception
adapters remain open. Initial native
EQS graph and typed provider authoring is implemented below. Generic reflected
properties do not substitute for those graph or runtime adapters.

Add support for:

- Behavior Trees: root/task/service/decorator graph inspection, node creation,
  deletion, links, properties, layout, compile/validation, and blackboard
  compatibility.
- Blackboards: key inspection, add/rename/delete, key type, base blackboard,
  category, instance-editable flags, and validation.
- StateTree assets: state, transition, task, condition, evaluator, parameter,
  and link editing where the installed UE modules expose public editor APIs.
- Environment Query assets: query generators, tests, options, parameters,
  graph/layout, and validation.
- AI Perception configuration and data assets where they are represented by
  editable assets rather than actor/component properties.

Proposed route families:

- `/behavior-trees/inspect`, `/behavior-trees/nodes`, `/behavior-trees/links`,
  `/behavior-trees/layout`, `/behavior-trees/compile`, `/behavior-trees/validate`.
- `/blackboards/inspect`, `/blackboards/keys`, `/blackboards/validate`.
- `/state-trees/inspect`, `/state-trees/states`, `/state-trees/transitions`,
  `/state-trees/tasks`, `/state-trees/validate`.
- `/environment-queries/inspect`, `/environment-queries/options`,
  `/environment-queries/tests`, `/environment-queries/validate`.

### Native StateTree Authoring

Implemented native `UStateTree` authoring with owned editor data/schema, stable
state/node/transition GUIDs and native compilation. Routes:

- `GET /state-trees/inspect`, `GET /state-trees/validate` (compile a transient copy).
- `POST /state-trees/create`, `POST/PATCH/DELETE /state-trees/states`,
  `POST /state-trees/move`, `POST/PATCH/DELETE /state-trees/transitions`.
- `POST/PATCH/DELETE /state-trees/nodes`, `POST /state-trees/compile`.

Nodes support schema-approved native struct tasks, global tasks, evaluators,
enter conditions and transition conditions. Settings use bounded editable scalar
or plain-struct UE text values and native clamps. Transition configuration covers
native targets, registered event tags, priority, enabled state and bounded delay.
Condition input fields still require bindings when the native compiler demands
them; unbound input defaults do not bypass compiler validation.

Edits require an idle editor and `/Game` assets. Every edit compiles a transient
preflight before changing the source. Preview duplication restores canonical owned
editor GUIDs because native duplication normally regenerates them. Source edits
use native transactions and compile caches are refreshed after undo/redo. Guards
cover hierarchy cycles, ownership, capacities, dangling targets, unsupported
node instances and binding-sensitive deletions; deletion requires confirmation.
Dry-run, no-op detection and optional save are exposed through REST and MCP tools.

Verified on UE 5.7.1: `UE5MCP.StateTree.Authoring` executes the actual native
state machine, checks transition completion, edited task timing and condition
selection before/after undo and redo. HTTP smoke coverage checks state/node/
transition lifecycle, order, rename, rejected input and source preservation.
A fresh editor reload confirms exact identities/order/settings, compiled state
data/hash and clean package state. Temporary fixtures were deleted.

Still pending: reference/container parameters, property functions and output bindings,
external linked assets,
Blueprint UObject node settings, single-task schemas, consideration authoring,
custom editor layouts, broader schema support and live PIE component controls.
This milestone does not close the full StateTree coverage requirement.

### StateTree Parameter Bags and Direct Bindings

Implemented root and state native `FInstancedPropertyBag` parameter inspection,
creation, value updates, rename and deletion via `POST/PATCH/DELETE
/state-trees/parameters`. StateId selects a state bag; empty selects root.
ItemId is the native field GUID. Field IDs survive rename, bag layout rebuilds,
undo/redo and cold reload. Supported types include native scalars, enums with
TypePath and plain native struct values with TypePath. Settings use bounded UE
text import and finite/native enum validation. Bags are limited to 64 fields;
reference/container types and type replacement remain pending.

`POST/DELETE /state-trees/bindings` adds/replaces/removes direct native property
bindings. Rows contain SourceId/SourcePath and TargetId/TargetPath. `root` aliases
the root parameter bag. `GET /state-trees/bindables?asset_path=...&target_id=...`
returns native accessible source descriptors and bounded property-name/type
metadata. Paths use native property syntax, at most 8 segments/256 characters.
Native target execution scope and compiler copy compatibility remain authoritative.
Bindings are limited to 1024, replacement/deletion require confirmation, and
attempted compiler pruning of invalid bindings fails preflight rather than
silently accepting a different edit.

Node creation/update accepts up to 64 atomic Bindings rows; `$new` addresses the
created/selected node. This lets required input bindings compile in the same
transaction as their node. Rename updates native cached parameter paths by field
GUID. Parameter deletion rejects referenced fields. Node/state/transition deletion
removes bindings targeting removed nodes, but rejects sources consumed by surviving
nodes. All operations retain transient preflight, dry-run, no-op and save behavior.

The editor-data object is explicitly transactional so root bags and bindings
restore alongside states. Undo refresh includes parameter values in its signature,
recompiles changed native data and resolves transient binding copy paths even when
a serialized editor hash is unchanged. This prevents stale shared instance data
and missing copy-property pointers during execution.

Verified on UE 5.7.1: native runtime Bool Compare selection from root/state bags,
parameter value changes and rename, undo/redo execution, guarded parameter deletion,
and binding cleanup/restoration after node deletion. HTTP verifies typed scalar/
enum/vector defaults, atomic required inputs, direct binding lifecycle, type/scope/
missing-path guards, dry-run/no-op, field rename and transactions. A fresh editor
reload preserves field GUIDs/types/values, root/state bags, binding paths, compiled
hashes and clean package state. Temporary test assets were deleted. MCP tools expose
parameter, binding and accessible-source operations.

Cross-asset links are implemented below. Still open:
reference/container parameters, type replacement, property functions/output
bindings, Blueprint node instances, single-task schemas, considerations and live
PIE component controls. This is partial StateTree coverage.

### Local Linked StateTree Subtrees

Implemented native `Linked` state creation using TargetStateId to an owned
`Subtree`, and `POST /state-trees/links` to retarget an existing linked state.
Retarget requires confirmation and preserves the linked state's GUID. Inspection
reports target GUID/name, inherited bag fields and parameter override GUIDs.
Linked states cannot own child states/tasks. Local selection-graph validation
checks hierarchy plus subtree-link edges for cycles and depth beyond 64 before
native compilation; transitions retain their separate native semantics. Deleting
a subtree referenced by surviving linked states is rejected.

Linked parameter layouts/names are inherited from the target subtree. Value
updates create native field-GUID overrides; default value/layout/name changes on
the target propagate while preserving overrides. `POST
/state-trees/parameters/reset` requires confirmation and calls the native override
reset, restoring the inherited default and removing its input binding. Direct
bindings targeting linked parameters mark the corresponding native override.
Native local bag migration and cached path refresh run before compiler validation,
so renamed inherited fields retain binding identities. All affected owned states
participate in the existing transaction and undo cache refresh.

Verified on UE 5.7.1: both `UE5MCP.StateTree` tests pass. The new linked-subtree test
runs the native state machine, measures task timing from inherited/overridden
parameters, resets defaults, retargets between different executing subtrees and
checks undo/redo runtime behavior. Guards include direct and mutually linked
subtree cycles, deletion references and source preservation. HTTP verifies local
link creation, inherited layout/value/name propagation, override/reset/binding
cleanup, retarget, fixed-layout guards, undo and save. Fresh editor reload preserves
linked target GUID/name, field IDs/defaults/overrides, paths and clean compiled hash.
Test fixtures were deleted. MCP exposes linked creation, retarget and parameter
reset.

Cross-asset dependency handling is implemented below. Other pending StateTree
areas above remain open.

### Cross-Asset Linked StateTrees and Caller Propagation

Implemented `LinkedAsset` state creation with LinkedAssetPath and existing
`POST /state-trees/links` retargeting. Linked targets require owned native editor
data and the same schema class. Inspection includes the asset path and inherited
parameter fields/override IDs. Value overrides, reset and direct bindings use the
same native APIs as local links. Empty inherited bags clear obsolete override IDs.

Edits discover registered and loaded callers, including unsaved assets, and
capture the transitive caller set. Caller discovery is bounded to 256 assets;
each operation supports up to 64 related assets, dependency depth 16, 4096 states
and 8192 nodes in total. Cycles and noneditable affected callers are rejected.
Unchanged forward dependencies must have current compiled data. Native schema,
parameter layout and binding compatibility remain authoritative.

Preflight clones the affected callers and their forward dependencies, restores
canonical editor identities and remaps all linked asset pointers to corresponding
copies. Copies compile in dependency order with the exported native compiler,
without compile-manager completion broadcasts. This prevents preview compilation
from migrating source callers' bags. Invalid binding pruning fails preflight.
Successful source edits capture every affected asset/editor data/schema/state in
one native transaction, compile dependencies before callers through the native
compiler manager, refresh native caches and notify editors. Undo/redo refreshes
tracked dependency closures in topological order, including resolved binding paths.

Mutation responses include affected_assets. Dry-run reports the same caller set;
no-op/dry-run preserve all source assets. Save explicitly saves all affected assets,
and reports failure if any save fails. MCP StateTree calls use extended timeouts
for dependency compilation. Parameter rename/default/layout changes propagate to
caller bags while retaining field GUID overrides and compatible bindings.

Verified on UE 5.7.1: all three `UE5MCP.StateTree` tests pass. The asset-link test
executes three native linked frames, checks inherited task timing, root edits and
transitive caller capture, caller overrides, rename/reset, actual alternate-asset
retargeting, undo/redo and source preservation for dry-run/validation/cycle rejection.
HTTP checks linked creation/retarget, affected caller sets, grouped undo/redo,
layout/default/name propagation, fixed-layout rules, schema/self/transitive cycle
guards and graph save. A fresh editor reload preserves linked references, field
GUIDs/defaults/overrides, bindings, compiled hashes and clean packages; read-only
validation preserves every source. Temporary fixtures were deleted.

Still open: native reference/container parameter adapters and type replacement,
property functions/output bindings, Blueprint node instances, single-task schemas,
considerations, broader schema/context compatibility and live PIE component controls.
This remains partial StateTree coverage and does not close the full plan.

### Typed StateTree Reference Parameters

Implemented Object, Class, SoftObject and SoftClass parameters using TypePath as
an explicit class constraint. Creation and value updates call native property-bag
setters. Values use full persistent asset or native/generated class paths; empty
or None clears the value. Asset existence and class compatibility are validated
before mutation. Native script classes are supported even when their engine object
flags include Transient; transient generated classes, stale classes, actor instances
and subobject paths are rejected. Soft values retain native soft paths after
validation. Inspection includes reference_path alongside native exported value text.

Existing parameter rename, stable field GUIDs, direct binding, linked parameter
override/reset, isolated dependency preflight, grouped transactions and save apply
to references. Containers and parameter type replacement remain pending.

Verified on UE 5.7.1: all four StateTree automation tests pass. The reference test
binds object and class parameters into native Object Class Is condition execution,
checks selection after class changes/object clear and undo/redo, validates soft
paths and rejects missing/incompatible values without source changes. HTTP tests
cover all four reference types, native and generated Blueprint classes and class
constraints, direct bindings, null/rename, caller overrides/reset, invalid paths,
transactions and save. Fresh-editor reload preserves constraints, canonical paths,
bindings, inherited fields, clean packages and compiled hashes. Test assets and
Blueprint fixtures were deleted.

### Native StateTree Utility Considerations

The existing node routes and MCP node tool now accept Kind=consideration for
schema-approved native consideration structs. Inspection exposes each state's
considerations, IDs, configuration and instance values. Creation/update/deletion
retain binding support, transient dependency preflight, transactions and save.
Weight is also available through the state property whitelist. Schema utility
permission and native scalar clamps are enforced.

Verified on UE 5.7.1: the editor build succeeds and
`UE5MCP.StateTree.UtilityConsiderations` passes. It runs a tree with native
highest-utility selection, verifies changing a Constant consideration switches the
selected child, checks undo/redo runtime selection, rejects an out-of-range score
without changing source, restores a deleted consideration through undo and checks
read-only validation preserves source. HTTP consideration coverage now verifies bound scores, node lifecycle, state weight
edits, invalid score/type guards, dry-run/no-op, deletion/binding restoration and
save. A fresh editor reload preserves consideration IDs/settings/bindings, highest
utility selection policy, weights, clean package state and compiled hash. Read-only
validation preserves the source; temporary fixtures were deleted. Custom
response-curve/enum-score settings remain pending.

### StateTree Expression Update Controls

Node updates now accept bSetExpression to explicitly replace native operand and
indentation for enter conditions, transition conditions and considerations. MCP
exposes set_expression. Ordinary node-setting updates preserve expression fields.
Indentation uses the native MaxExpressionIndent limit (4), avoiding silent compiler
clamping of values 5-8 previously accepted by the adapter. The native compiler
remains authoritative for expression execution. The build and
`UE5MCP.StateTree.Expressions` pass: native AND/OR updates switch selected children,
undo/redo restores behavior, invalid indentation/hidden operands reject without
source changes, and transient validation preserves source. The expanded native test distinguishes flat and nested AND/OR grouping and
checks undo/redo selection. HTTP verifies operand/indent updates, unchanged grouping
on ordinary settings edits, guards, dry-run/no-op, transactions and save. Fresh
editor reload preserves IDs, operands, indentation, clean package state and compiled
hash. Read-only validation preserves source and fixtures were deleted. Broader
transition-condition and consideration expression runtime combinations remain open.

### StateTree Native Node Discovery

`GET /state-trees/node-types` and MCP list_state_tree_node_types enumerate loaded
native script structs approved by an existing asset's schema. Kind selects task,
global_task, condition, evaluator or consideration. Search is bounded to 128
characters and limit to 1-256; sorted results include total/truncated metadata.
Results report instance types, editable field names/types/categories, native clamps
and whether scalar/plain-struct settings are supported. Schema restrictions on
evaluators and utility considerations apply. The response explicitly identifies
its loaded-native scope; unloaded optional modules and Blueprint UObject nodes
are not enumerated. Fields with Input category may still require native bindings.

Verified: UE 5.7.1 build and HTTP discovery checks pass for Delay tasks, Random
conditions and Constant considerations, including native clamp metadata, filtering,
limits, invalid input and exact source preservation. Temporary fixture deleted.

### StateTree Schema Restriction Guards

Inspection now reports schema_capabilities for multiple tasks, enter conditions,
evaluators, considerations, global parameters, task completion and scheduled
ticking. Creation rejects schema-disallowed state types. Parameter edits reject
root parameters when the schema disallows them. State settings reject disallowed
selection rules, schema-fixed completion settings and unsupported scheduled tick
settings. Linked/LinkedAsset selection must remain TryEnterState; other requested
rules are rejected instead of being silently replaced by the native compiler.

Verified on UE 5.7.1: editor build and all six StateTree automation tests pass.
The linked-subtree test explicitly checks rejection and exact source preservation
for a selection setting the compiler would override. Other schema-specific guards
follow native schema APIs; broader optional-schema fixtures remain pending.

### StateTree PIE Component Inspection

`GET /state-trees/runtime` and MCP inspect_state_tree_runtime list native StateTree
components in the explicitly selected PIE world, or inspect one component_path.
Results include native run status, running/paused/registered flags, owner authority,
component/schema paths and debug active-state names when the engine build supports
them. Names are labels, not unique identifiers across linked assets. Search and
limits are bounded; stale/wrong-world paths and inactive PIE are rejected.
The adapter performs no runtime or authored-asset mutations.

Verified: UE 5.7.1 build, Python syntax and actual owned PIE lifecycle HTTP tests
pass for inactive/start/stop, empty listing/search, invalid limits, nonexistent
world and stale component path. The default map contained zero StateTree components;
A separate `UE5MCP.StateTree.RuntimePIE` native automation fixture now passes with
an owned running component in an actual PIE world. It verifies exact component and
owner paths, native Running status/authority, active Waiting state, paused/resumed/
stopped flags, destroyed-component rejection and exact authored-source preservation.
The fixture starts/stops its owned PIE session and removes its unsaved test asset.
Runtime control routes and event/parameter operations remain pending; the native
pause/resume/stop calls above are fixture actions, not newly exposed API controls.

### StateTree Native PIE Lifecycle Controls

`POST /state-trees/runtime` and MCP control_state_tree_runtime expose native
start/restart/stop/pause/resume for an explicit registered authoritative component
in the selected PIE world. Reason text is bounded. Start/restart require a ready
native tree reference. Repeated start on running, pause on paused, resume on
unpaused and stop on stopped logic are no-ops; pause/resume require running logic.
Restart always requests native restart. Responses report applied/would_change,
dry_run and resulting native status/flags. Dry-run performs validation only.
These controls do not author assets or create editor transactions.

Verified on UE 5.7.1: editor build and RuntimePIE automation pass using the new
control entry point for dry-run, repeated pause/no-op, resume, restart and stop on
a real running component, with exact authored-source preservation. The expanded running PIE fixture also verifies start-from-stopped, start dry-run,
repeated start/stop no-ops, pause-on-stopped rejection and wrong-world/asset-path/
invalid-operation/destroyed-target guards while retaining running state on rejected
requests. The build and RuntimePIE test pass. The fixture now sends an asynchronous HTTP POST through the actual local server
to pause the live component, verifies HTTP 200/applied/paused and the native paused
flag, then resumes and completes lifecycle checks. Build and RuntimePIE pass with
this successful transport-level dispatch. The test uses the configured API port
and the HTTP client module. Runtime events/parameter changes remain open.

### StateTree Runtime Events

Runtime control Operation=event and MCP send_state_tree_event submit registered
Gameplay Tag events to explicit registered authoritative PIE components. Logic must
be running and unpaused. Optional StructPath/Properties specify a native payload
struct <=64KiB with plain scalar/struct fields and bounded editable UE text settings;
Name supplies an origin label <=128 characters. Native clamps/finite checks apply.
Dry-run validates but sends nothing. event_submitted means the native void send API
was invoked. event_queue_accepted reports an observed single native queue append
matching tag, origin, payload type and contents; it does not acknowledge a transition
or payload-field consumption. Before/after queue counts and queued payload type are
reported. Native queue capacity is checked before sending, including dry-run; full
queues reject without mutation. Callers inspect runtime state to observe effects.

Verified on UE 5.7.1: build and RuntimePIE test pass with a temporary registered tag,
authored native OnEvent transition, dry-run preservation, unknown-tag rejection,
native transition to success and exact authored-source preservation. Owned tag
configuration and unsaved asset fixtures are cleaned up with the PIE session.
The expanded RuntimePIE fixture also passes with an actual HTTP event carrying a
native payload: native clamp rejection, payload dry-run, HTTP 200/submission, observed
queue acceptance/type and subsequent tag-based transition to success are verified.
It fills the owned native queue to capacity and checks rejection without modifying
the full queue before clearing it for the valid event. Authored source remains
unchanged. Binding a payload field into transition/node execution still requires a
dedicated fixture; the current transition matches the tag.
Runtime parameter changes remain pending.

### StateTree Component Reference Parameters

Runtime Operation=parameters and MCP set_state_tree_runtime_parameters update
existing parameters on a stopped authoritative PIE component's FStateTreeReference.
Properties maps names to supported scalar/plain-struct UE text or typed persistent
reference paths. Updates prepare a reference copy, validate every setting, mark
native field-GUID overrides and apply through SetStateTreeReference. Reset via
Operation=reset_parameter/Name removes one override and inherits the asset default.
Running or paused logic must be explicitly stopped first; no automatic stop/restart,
asset mutation or editor transaction is performed. Changes take effect on next start.
Dry-run and no-op comparison use the prepared reference without applying it.

Runtime inspection includes tree_asset, reference synchronization state,
reference_parameters and reference_parameter_overrides. Inspection synchronizes a
copy to avoid mutating the component as a read side effect.

Verified on UE 5.7.1: build and RuntimePIE pass. A root parameter bound to native
Delay duration is overridden on the stopped component, started, and observed to
complete through the expected native completion transition. The test checks dry-run,
repeat no-op, unknown/nonfinite settings rejection, running-edit rejection, reset to
inherited value and exact authored-source preservation. The fixture now sends the parameter update through actual HTTP POST, verifies
HTTP 200/applied/parameter_operation, inspects the changed native reference value
and starts it to observe completion. A mixed valid/invalid batch is rejected while
preserving the prior override. Build and RuntimePIE pass with this transport-level
coverage. Broader reference/container runtime combinations remain open.

### Parameter Type and Container Implementation — Untested

Feature-first changes add confirmation-guarded parameter type replacement while
retaining field identity/name and using native property-bag migration. Optional
initial values are applied before existing dependency/binding preflight. Array/Set
container descriptors are supported on creation and replacement. Values use JSON
arrays of typed strings, with at most 256 elements, <=64KiB text and <=1MiB native
element storage per value. Native scalar/enum/plain-struct/persistent-reference
validation is reused per element. Sets require hashing and use native deduplication.
Inspection reports kind, size, typed element strings and truncation flags. Native
parameter field reordering is available through `/state-trees/parameters/move`
and MCP `move_state_tree_parameter`, retaining identities and values. Runtime
and linked overrides reuse these setters; parameter value no-op comparison uses
native property equality, including unordered set equality.

**Not built or tested.** Follow UNTESTED_FEATURES.md for migration, binding,
caller override, undo/redo, runtime, REST and cold persistence checks. Nested
containers and generic node-instance container settings remain unimplemented.

### Native Behavior Tree Graph Authoring

`GET /behavior-trees/inspect` now retains asset/Blackboard/root metadata and
reports the native editor graph, stable node GUIDs, composite/task/service/
decorator instances, parent attachments, pins, editable scalar/plain-struct UE
text properties, native selector/value-binding fields and validation. Inspection
does not create a missing graph. `POST /behavior-trees/graph` explicitly
initializes one using the native schema and graph APIs, preserving the asset's
Blackboard instead of adopting an arbitrary loaded Blackboard. Existing runtime
roots, children, services and root decorators are preserved.

`POST/PATCH/DELETE /behavior-trees/nodes` creates concrete native or compiled
Blueprint node classes, edits node settings/key bindings and deletes nodes.
Services/decorators require a composite/task parent; ordinary nodes connect via
`POST/DELETE /behavior-trees/links`. Native schema checks govern pin kinds,
cycles, multiple parents and root constraints. Replacing links requires
confirmation; delete dry-runs report attached subnodes and affected neighbors.
Deletion removes the selected node and attached subnodes, leaving linked children
as disconnected graph nodes. Root/read-only/injected nodes are protected.

`PATCH /behavior-trees/settings` sets/clears the root and compiled-tree
Blackboard together, with confirmation. Native key selectors are checked against
the selected key's concrete native filters. UE 5.7 ValueOrBBKey fields can bind to
compatible keys or clear the binding to use their stored fallback. Node property
values are preflighted on a transient duplicate; only top-level editable scalars
and plain structs without UObject/container traversal are imported. Native numeric
ClampMin/ClampMax, finite +/-1e12 bounds and import errors are checked. Requests
accept at most 64 properties/32 bindings and text values of 4096 code units.
Missing, skeleton, stale or failed Blueprint node classes are rejected.

`POST /behavior-trees/layout` sets explicit top-level positions within +/-1e6;
it does not call the native auto-layout method, which requires Slate widgets.
X coordinates affect native sibling execution order. `POST /behavior-trees/compile`
uses the native graph rebuild. Every mutation refreshes native execution data,
uses a scoped transaction, supports dry-run/save, and rejects PIE/simulation or
non-/Game assets. Graphs are bounded to 512 nodes and depth 64; prospective link
depth is checked before changes. Ownership validation prevents native rebuilds
from moving foreign runtime node objects. Runtime-only tree initialization is
preflighted for missing/shared/foreign nodes and capacity before graph creation.

Initial graph construction uses a short transaction-recording guard after the
asset and preexisting runtime nodes have been recorded. The completed graph
reference participates in undo; its partial construction does not. Native graph
updates remain locked until construction finishes. This avoids a detached graph's
native PostEditUndo clearing the restored runtime-only tree, and avoids partial
subnode updates losing existing services/decorators. No plugin-defined graph
asset class or global undo hook is introduced.

`GET /behavior-trees/validate` and the existing POST validation route return
bounded topology, root, disconnected-node, ownership and direct key-compatibility
checks. Native execution indexes and resolved selector IDs are transient caches;
inspection labels this explicitly. Persisted `compiled_children`, decorator
operations, `compiled_services` and root decorators report authoritative runtime
child/auxiliary order independently of those caches. Read-only validation derives
reachability from graph links and checks selector compatibility on copies. It does
not mutate the source to refresh caches or imply arbitrary task runtime success.

The UE 5.7 target builds with the required AIGraph dependency. Native automation
`UE5MCP.BehaviorTree.GraphRuntime` passed initialization/undo/redo over an existing
runtime root/task/service/root decorator, preservation of object ownership and
Blackboard, native compiled child/service/decorator arrays, rejected incompatible
value binding without source changes, branch deletion/undo/redo, and X-position
execution-order changes/undo. An owned transient Game world initialized a real
AIController, BlackboardComponent and single-run BehaviorTreeComponent: a Wait
bound to a Float key completed and a native Set Bool Key task wrote the marker.

The REST fixture passed composite/task/service/decorator CRUD, scalar/plain-struct
settings, native selector and value-binding compatibility, rejection preservation,
root/pin/schema/reparent/confirmation guards, headless layout and child order,
compile/save, attached-subnode deletion/undo/redo, dry-run/no-op and PIE guards.
A fresh editor passed stable GUIDs, links, attachments, properties, selected key
names and persisted native child/decorator/service order with a clean package.
Explicit compile then refreshed transient indexes to the expected native order.
Owned fixtures were removed. The first REST attempt supplied the Finish task's
Enum value-binding field as a scalar; that field is outside the plain-struct
adapter, so the test now uses its native successful default. This does not claim
Enum/provider editing support that has not been implemented.

UObject/container/custom provider settings (including Enum value-binding defaults),
Blueprint-node cold/runtime coverage, and broader runtime/controller authority
workflows remain separate adapters/gates. Existing graph mutations do not replace
those missing capabilities.

### Simple Parallel Behavior Tree Nodes

Behavior Tree node creation now maps native SimpleParallel classes to
`UBehaviorTreeGraphNode_SimpleParallel`, preserving its distinct native pins.
Output 0 accepts exactly one main task; output 1 accepts one background task or
composite branch. The native compiler emits these roles as child slots 0 and 1,
independent of the two branches' X positions. Ordinary sibling sorting still
applies within each branch/output pin. Inspection adds a `parallel` object with
finish mode and main/background GUIDs alongside authoritative compiled children.

`FinishMode` uses the existing scalar property adapter with native values
`AbortBackground` and `WaitForBackground`. Native enum values and generated MAX
sentinels are checked before property mutation. Validation reports missing main
or background pins, a non-task main, an invalid finish mode and mismatches between
the graph roles and compiled native child slots. Incomplete authoring can be
inspected/saved, but is not reported ready. Native schema replacement guards,
transactions, undo/redo, dry-run/no-op, save and existing PIE restrictions apply.
No synthetic background node is added to hide an incomplete graph.

The UE 5.7 editor target built successfully. Native automation
`UE5MCP.BehaviorTree.SimpleParallel` verified the specialized graph class,
main-task/composite-background compilation despite reversed X positions,
incomplete validation, schema rejection without source changes and invalid enum
rejection. Separate owned transient Game worlds initialized native controllers,
Blackboards and single-run BehaviorTreeComponents for each mode. A short main
Wait and longer background Wait followed by a Set Bool Key task verified immediate
background abortion (marker remains false) and delayed background completion
(marker becomes true). The delayed case required more native component ticks.

The REST fixture passed specialized pins, main/background metadata and compiled
roles, attached service/decorator data, main-composite rejection, finish-mode
preflight/dry-run/no-op/undo/redo, missing-main validation, background replacement
confirmation and undo, role preservation across X-layout changes and compile/save.
A fresh editor passed saved graph class, pin roles, finish mode, native child and
auxiliary order, and clean-package state; owned fixtures were removed. An
approval-review usage limit temporarily prevented the first test editor launch.
The later launch succeeded through the normal approval path before these runtime
and persistence results were recorded. Blueprint-derived parallel classes and
subtree-injection/compound-logic combinations need separate fixtures.

### Static Run Behavior Subtrees

`BTTask_RunBehavior` creation now uses the native specialized subtree graph node.
Node create/update accepts `bSetSubtree/SubtreePath`; the MCP wrappers expose
`subtree_path` (None preserves, empty clears). The protected native BehaviorAsset
reference is edited through a typed adapter, without enabling generic UObject
property traversal. Missing references remain inspectable incomplete authoring.
References require persistent assets with compiled roots. Referenced root
decorators require an initialized editor graph. Both classic decorators and
compound root expressions use the native injection path described below.

Preflight traverses prospective static dependencies before changes, including
replacement/removal of the edited task. It rejects cycles, depth beyond 32,
more than 256 assets/1024 visits, incompatible Blackboards and mismatched key IDs
or native declared key filters. A transient diagnostic BlackboardComponent uses
the native compatibility predicate; the additional ID/filter checks prevent the
native local-key-equality fallback from accepting incompatible inherited layouts.
Referenced compiled nodes are checked for key bindings and incomplete parallel
roles/unconfigured nested RunBehavior tasks. Injection capacity must fit the
existing 512-node parent limit. RunBehavior is rejected on a SimpleParallel main
pin because the native parent cannot push a subtree there.

The native graph injection API creates read-only previews of referenced root
decorators. Source decorators' temporary native copy/ownership operations are
excluded from the parent's transaction history. Refresh invalidates the native
short-name cache so equal-named assets in separate packages cannot reuse stale
previews. Injected API GUIDs combine the owning task GUID with the native copied
GUID; native GUIDs are unchanged. This gives distinct, stable inspection IDs for
multiple calls to the same subtree, including after cold reload and refresh.
Injected nodes cannot be edited, linked or deleted individually. Their native
runtime counts and editor preview counts are exposed in each task's `subtree`
metadata.

Derived previews are recorded through parent graph/subnode arrays. Individual
injected nodes are excluded from transaction recording: the initial REST redo
check found that their native PostEditUndo could reinsert old previews alongside
replacements. The fix passed native and REST undo/redo regressions. Asset edits
remain forbidden during PIE/simulation; this implements static RunBehavior
references and does not expose runtime RunBehaviorDynamic replacement.

The UE 5.7 target built. Native automation `UE5MCP.BehaviorTree.Subtree` passed
repeated calls to one decorated subtree, unique/read-only preview IDs, source
snapshot preservation, cycle rejection without parent changes, reference clear
undo/redo, and repeated native refresh. Owned transient Game worlds initialized
real controllers, Blackboards and single-run BehaviorTreeComponents: an injected
Bool root-decorator gate blocked the child marker and parent continuation when
false, and allowed both when true.

The REST fixture passed typed creation/reference update/clear, two callers of one
subtree, same-short-name source switching with different decorator classes,
inherited Blackboard compatibility, self/indirect-cycle and mismatch rejection,
read-only preview guards, source preservation, dry-run/no-op and undo/redo. A fresh
editor passed persisted references, preview IDs/flags, native counts and compiled
roles with clean source packages. Explicit refresh kept scoped IDs stable and
preserved both referenced source snapshots; owned fixtures were removed. Dynamic
runtime substitution, Blueprint-derived subtree tasks and
large/deep dependency boundary fixtures remain open.

### Compound Decorator Expressions

`POST /behavior-trees/decorator-logic` attaches a native compound decorator to
an existing composite/task. `PATCH` replaces its whole prefix expression and
optionally its name. MCP exposes `create_behavior_tree_decorator_logic` and
`replace_behavior_tree_decorator_logic`. Prefix rows use `Operation` with
AND/OR `Children` 2–16, NOT `Children` 1, or TEST `ClassPath`, `Properties` and
`BlackboardSelectors`. Leaf settings use the existing typed preflight; replacing
an expression starts each leaf from native class defaults.

The native decorator graph/schema owns the sink, logic nodes, test nodes and
pins. Inspection includes inner GUIDs, positions, links, leaf classes/settings,
Blackboard key names and collected native prefix operations. Compiled decorator
references resolve to the corresponding inner node GUIDs. Graph validation
checks ownership, symmetric internal links, reachability, cycles, pin arities
and unique inner IDs before calling native collection. Limits are 127 prefix
rows, 64 tests, depth 16, 1,024 total editor nodes and 511 runtime instances.
Dry-run, no-op, save and existing PIE guards apply. New immutable inner graphs
are swapped inside the existing transaction; native undo restores leaf ownership.

The native `UE5MCP.BehaviorTree.Compound` test passed all eight actual controller /
Blackboard / single-run component cases for `OR(AND(A,B),NOT(C))`, native test/op
counts, equivalent replacement, trailing-operand rejection and replacement
undo/redo. The REST fixture passed dry-run/no-op, invalid arity/missing key/trailing
operand rejection, replacement, delete/undo and save. A fresh editor matched
persisted inner GUIDs/pins, leaf settings, names, native operations and compiled
references with a clean package. Owned fixtures were removed.

Blueprint-derived leaf runtime coverage, arbitrary inner-node editing and compound/SimpleParallel
combinations remain separate gates.

### Compound Root Decorators in Static Subtrees

RunBehavior references now accept compiled compound root expressions. Before
native copying, preflight flattens the source root groups, adjusts test indexes,
adds the native AND wrapper for multiple groups, and requires exact agreement
with the source runtime decorator instances and operation array. Existing
Blackboard, dependency, ownership and PIE guards apply. Capacity checks include
owned and injected compound inner graphs and runtime leaves (512 outer nodes,
1,024 total editor nodes and 511 runtime instances).

Native injection copies the bound graph and marks the wrapper/graph read-only.
Inner API IDs combine their native GUID with the owning injected wrapper ID,
which already includes the caller GUID. Repeated references therefore expose
unique IDs without changing engine GUIDs. Native compound copy restoration
renames source leaves; the adapter records and restores their original names
and owners outside transaction recording, preserving referenced source identities.

`UE5MCP.BehaviorTree.CompoundSubtree` passed native repeated-reference inspection,
scoped inner IDs, source snapshots, cycle rejection, reference clear/undo/redo,
and actual single-run nested execution: the compound root gate blocked both
child markers and parent continuation when false and allowed them when true.
The REST fixture passed compound-to-classic same-short-name source switching,
inherited Blackboard compatibility, invalid/read-only guards, source preservation,
dry-run/no-op, undo/redo and save. A fresh editor matched source/parent snapshots
and clean package state; explicit refresh preserved scoped outer/inner IDs and
source snapshots. Owned fixtures were removed.

Dynamic runtime subtree replacement, Blueprint-derived task/leaf execution and
large/deep dependency boundary fixtures remain separate gates.

### Dynamic Subtree Defaults and Injection Tags

Native `BTTask_RunBehaviorDynamic` nodes use the existing node create/update
routes with `bSetSubtree`/`SubtreePath` for `DefaultBehaviorAsset` and
`bSetInjectionTag`/`InjectionTag` for the tag. MCP node helpers expose
`subtree_path` and `injection_tag`: None preserves a field, empty clears it.
Inspection exposes `dynamic_subtree.default_asset_path`, `injection_tag` and
`tag_registered`. Defaults remain optional for runtime injection; missing tags
are reported as incomplete authoring. Nonempty tag input must already exist in
the Gameplay Tags dictionary. Generic property writes cannot bypass this typed
tag control, including case variants.

Prospective dependency checks include dynamic default references alongside
static references, with the same persistent compiled-root, ownership, Blackboard,
cycle and capacity guards. Dynamic defaults with root decorators are rejected
because native RunBehaviorDynamic ignores those decorators. Both subtree task
types are rejected on SimpleParallel's main-task pin, where native CanPushSubtree
returns false. Asset edits retain transactions, dry-run, no-op, save and PIE guards.

The native `UE5MCP.BehaviorTree.Dynamic` test passed default replacement undo/redo,
registered-tag and cycle preflight, and actual controller/Blackboard/component
execution. The default wait-and-marker subtree completed normally. Native
SetDynamicSubtree during that active wait aborted its marker and executed the
replacement marker, while the authored default reference remained unchanged.
The first fixture used a native tag in an editor-only module and triggered an
engine startup ensure; it was replaced with an owned temporary tag ini search
path. The rerun passed without that startup error, and the fixture removed its
configuration afterward.

The REST fixture passed typed defaults/tags, dry-run/no-op, unknown tag and generic
property bypass rejection, decorated-default/cycle/main-pin rejection, clearing
and undo/redo. A fresh editor matched persisted default references, registered
tags, native task graph and source settings with clean packages. Owned assets
and the temporary project tag configuration were removed.

Live PIE controls are described below. Blueprint-derived runtime coverage remains
open. Asset authoring routes do not invoke runtime SetDynamicSubtree.

### Live Behavior Tree Components and Dynamic Replacement

`GET /behavior-trees/runtime` discovers registered components in the selected
PIE world (`pie_instance`, default -1 requires an unambiguous world). Optional
`component_path` selects one component. Inspection reports owner/authority,
running/paused state, root/current asset, instantiated dynamic task template and
instance paths, stack/execution indexes, injection tag, default and current asset.
Discovery is bounded to 256 components and 512 dynamic instances per component.

`POST /behavior-trees/runtime/dynamic-subtree` takes `ComponentPath`,
`InjectionTag`, `AssetPath`, `PIEInstance` and `bDryRun`. It requires an explicit
registered component in that PIE world, a live authoritative owner, a running
unpaused tree, and an exact registered tag matching an instantiated dynamic task.
Empty AssetPath disables the subtree. No-op and dry-run do not invoke the native
setter. Responses report matched/would-change counts and whether the native
update was submitted. MCP exposes `inspect_behavior_tree_runtime` and
`replace_behavior_tree_runtime_subtree`.

Preflight resolves current instance overrides and prospective replacements while
walking the effective tree. It checks persistent compiled assets, source/native
ownership and topology, actual live Blackboard IDs/types and selectors, static
and dynamic dependency cycles, ignored dynamic root decorators, configured static
tasks, registered dynamic tags and native parallel roles. Limits remain depth
32, 256 assets/1,024 dependency visits, and bounded per-tree traversal. Ambiguous
current overrides for a shared native template reject before mutation. Trees
without Blackboards remain supported when their nodes require no Blackboard.

The setter uses native SetDynamicSubtree. Active replacement requests restart
asynchronously; submission is not an execution-completion claim. Clearing an
active subtree can fail its branch. Only currently instantiated matching tasks
change; newly created task instances use authored defaults. These runtime changes
create no asset edits, save operation or undo transaction, and inspection reads
native per-instance state without a plugin override cache.

All seven `UE5MCP.BehaviorTree.*` tests passed after the shared runtime changes.
The expanded Dynamic test covered real-controller no-op, dry-run, effective cycle
rejection, replacement and clear execution. RuntimePIE started an actual owned
PIE session, inspected its controller component, applied replacement/clear and
observed markers, and verified source preservation. It rejected wrong-world IDs,
asset-as-component targets, paused components, decorated candidates, mismatched
Blackboards and registered parent tags that did not exactly match. Repeated
replacement was a no-op. The initial PIE fixture asserted shutdown before native
asynchronous teardown completed; cleanup now waits for it, and the full rerun
passed. Fixtures and their temporary tag search paths were removed.

The HTTP fixture passed editor-only rejection, query validation, real PIE
component discovery, wrong-world/target guards and owned play-session cleanup.
Multiplayer client rejection and multiple simultaneous PIE-world fixtures,
Blueprint-derived task behavior and large/deep runtime boundary fixtures remain
separate coverage gates.

### Native Environment Query Authoring

EQS now has dedicated `/environment-queries/create`, `/inspect`, `/validate`,
`/graph`, `/options`, `/tests`, `/layout` and `/compile` routes and MCP helpers.
Creation uses a new /Game package; graph initialization preserves existing native
runtime options, generators and tests and supports undo/redo back to a runtime-only
asset. The EnvironmentQueryEditor plugin is declared as a dependency. Its native
editor classes are not exported for direct C++ linkage, so the adapter resolves
those reflected classes and invokes native virtual graph/schema operations through
exported UAIGraph/UAIGraphNode interfaces. It creates no replacement graph classes.

Options own real UEnvQueryOption/generator instances and connect through the native
schema. Unique X positions determine native fallback order. Tests use native
subnodes and support insertion/reordering, enable/disable, typed settings and
confirmed deletion. Compile rebuilds the actual native option/test arrays;
read-only inspection compares compiled identities/order with graph state. Disabled
tests remain authorable but are omitted from compiled arrays. Native generator
bAutoSortTests can reorder execution independently of author order.

Settings support editable scalar/plain-struct UE text and typed compatible class
references (including contexts). Float/Int/Bool data providers have separate
ProviderValues defaults and NamedParameters bindings through owned native
UAIDataProvider_QueryParams objects; empty parameter names clear bindings.
Inspection reports provider defaults, binding classes/names and authored named
parameter types, including disabled tests. Conflicting scalar types for the same
parameter name, foreign bindings, invalid classes/item types, invalid enum values,
non-finite/native-clamp violations and incompatible float/Boolean filter/scoring
modes reject before mutation. Numeric values are bounded to +/-1e12, text values
to 4096 characters, option positions to +/-1e6, and each request to 64 settings.
Graphs allow 64 options, 64 tests per option and 512 total tests. Existing /Game,
PIE, transaction, dry-run/no-op and optional-save controls apply. Test-class replacement uses explicit deletion/recreation. Generator-tree replacement
is described below.

`UE5MCP.EnvironmentQuery.Authoring` passed initialization preservation and
undo/redo, native arrays, test disable/undo/redo, numeric rejection and X-order
changes. Actual native RunInstantQuery executions in fresh AI worlds returned the
querier location and selected option 0 for MinimumDistance=0, fell back to option
1 for MinimumDistance=1, and returned to option 0 with the first test disabled.
This verifies native Float query-parameter binding and fallback behavior.

The REST fixture passed creation, native options/tests, scalar/context/provider
settings, Float/Int/Bool bindings, type-conflict rejection, no-op/dry-run, invalid
input/route-kind/duplicate-X/filter-mode guards, enabled/test-order/delete undo/redo
and save. A fresh editor matched graph GUIDs, fallback/test order, provider defaults
and bindings, authored parameter types and clean package state. Owned fixtures
were removed. The AI capability endpoint now reports the implemented EQS, Behavior
Tree and Blackboard adapters instead of stale generic-only descriptions.

Custom provider authoring, test-class migration, forced composite item layouts,
Blueprint node/context runtime gates, broader navigation/trace generators/tests,
large boundary fixtures remain open. Live request/result controls are described below.

### Nested EQS Composite Generators

Option creation accepts `bSetGeneratorTree` and `GeneratorTree`; the dedicated
`PATCH /environment-queries/generators` replaces a writable option's generator
hierarchy while preserving its native option identity, graph GUID and attached
tests. MCP option creation accepts `generator_tree`, and
`replace_environment_query_generators` replaces it. Prefix rows contain ClassPath,
Children and the existing typed Properties/Classes/ProviderValues/NamedParameters
maps. Composite rows require 1–16 children; leaves require zero. Omitted settings
start from native class defaults. Limits are depth 8, 127 generators and 256
settings per expression, and 512 generators across the query.

The adapter creates real native UEnvQueryGenerator_Composite instances. Children
remain directly owned beneath their parent generator, so native graph orphan
cleanup does not discard them. Preflight traverses ownership/shape/cycles before
calling native recursive validity/item-type helpers. Child item types must match
exactly; asynchronous children (including classes whose native defaults request
async behavior) and forced mixed memory layouts reject before native check/assert
paths. Native VerifyItemTypes runs bottom-up on transient candidates. Replacement
also checks compatibility with all attached tests. Query parameter type/ownership
checks include nested generators, and source graph initialization observes the
same hierarchy/capacity rules.

Inspection exposes actual native `generator_tree` classes, item types, order,
settings, providers and children, without inventing inner graph-node GUIDs for
owned generator objects. Compiled option/test references now include native graph
GUIDs alongside classes. Dry-run/no-op, existing transactions/save and PIE guards
apply. Native metadata-deprecated classes reject at preflight; the first composite
fixture used metadata-deprecated EnvQueryTest_Random and emitted engine errors.
