It now uses a supported distance test, and both EQS automation tests pass.

`UE5MCP.EnvironmentQuery.Composite` executed real native queries in fresh AI
worlds: nested location generators produced two items; replacement produced one;
undo/redo restored counts, ownership and native option/test identity. It also
passed no-op and invalid mixed-item/async/forced-layout/arity/trailing-row guards.
A read-only cycle fixture rejected before native recursion and restored an
unchanged source snapshot. The REST fixture passed expression creation/replacement,
compiled IDs, nested parameter conflicts, depth/metadata-deprecation guards,
dry-run/no-op, replacement and option delete/undo, and save.

A fresh editor matched nested native generator classes, ownership-validated child
order/item types, settings, typed child query parameters, graph GUIDs and compiled
identities with a clean package. Owned fixtures were removed, and the capability
endpoint reports matching-type composite support. Forced/mixed item layouts, async
composite execution, incremental inner-generator editing, custom providers,
Blueprint-derived generator runtime gates remain open. Live request controls are
described below.

### Live Native EQS Requests and Results

`GET /environment-queries/runtime/owners` lists actor paths/classes/authority in a
selected PIE world, with search and limit 1–256. `POST /environment-queries/runtime`
accepts Operation run/cancel/forget; run takes AssetPath, explicit OwnerPath,
optional RequestId, RunMode, Parameters, MaxItems, TimeoutSeconds, PIEInstance and
bDryRun. `GET /environment-queries/runtime` lists owned records in that world or
selects request_id. MCP exposes owner discovery, run, inspect and request control.

Requests require an authoritative live actor in an unambiguous/explicit PIE world
and a valid compiled native query graph. They use native PrepareQueryInstance /
RunQuery and completion delegates, retaining weak owner/world/manager/instance
references. Parameter rows use Name, Type float/int/bool and scalar-text Value.
Names must match actual compiled native QueryParams declarations; omitted values
use native collected defaults. Native integer defaults are decoded from their
stored float bits before SetIntParam; overrides use the corresponding native typed
setter. Unknown/duplicate names, type mismatch, invalid scalars, values beyond
+/-1e6 and unsupported run modes reject before submission. At most 64 parameter
rows are accepted per request.

Run modes are all_matching, single, random_best_5 and random_best_25. Records
report request/native IDs, state and native status, owner, selected option, item
type, total/returned/native counts, elapsed time and retained scores, locations
and actor paths where applicable. Single/random results follow the native
Blueprint wrapper's selected-first-item semantics. The editor EQS debugger can
retain additional candidates, which remain visible as native_item_count instead
of being returned as selected results. Dead actor items do not emit stale paths
or invalid location sentinels.

Storage allows 64 retained records and 16 running requests. MaxItems 1–512 caps
only retained output; native generators can produce more items. Wall-clock timeout
is 0.1–60 seconds, and terminal snapshots are retained for 120 seconds or until
forget. Native abort services cancellation/expiry/owner loss. World cleanup removes
its records; module shutdown aborts remaining owned work and unbinds delegates,
including debugger-retained native instances. Runtime work creates no asset edits
or undo transaction. Manager time slicing and abort do not preempt a synchronous
generator mid-call; these controls are not a hard generator work/memory budget.

All three UE5MCP.EnvironmentQuery.* tests passed. Runtime tests used native
asynchronous manager ticks in AI worlds and verified location results, Float
fallback changes, Boolean trace-filter changes, exact Int defaults/overrides
(three/five circle items), output truncation, single-result semantics, invalid
parameters, dry-run, cancellation/no-op, expiry, owner loss, world cleanup with ID
reuse and unchanged source snapshots. The initial single-result assertion exposed
debugger-retained candidates; selected-result handling now follows Unreal's native
Blueprint wrapper, and the rerun passed.

The HTTP fixture started actual owned PIE sessions, discovered authoritative
owners, ran queries, verified fallback/all four run modes/scores/locations and
result caps, rejected invalid owners/worlds/modes/types/values/names, checked
forget/no-op cancellation, preserved clean source snapshots, and confirmed no
records survived play-session cleanup. Owned source assets were removed.

Multiplayer/multiple-world fixtures, broader actor/custom-item snapshots,
Blueprint-derived runtime generators/tests/contexts, navigation/trace breadth,
large resource boundaries and custom provider parameter conventions remain
separate coverage gates.

### Blackboard Authoring Progress

`GET /blackboards/inspect` retains the existing local `keys` array and adds
inherited entries with owning asset, native cached key ID, key-object path,
category, description, synchronization flag, package state and structural
validation. `GET /blackboards/validate` exposes the same structural report.
`POST/PATCH/DELETE /blackboards/keys` supports local key creation, rename,
concrete key-type replacement, metadata/synchronization updates and deletion.
`PATCH /blackboards/settings` sets or clears a parent. All new mutation paths
reject PIE/simulation, support dry-run/no-op/save, transact before changing data,
and use native parent/key-ID/synchronization updates. The old delete adapter's
mutation-before-Modify ordering is fixed.

Names use native case-insensitive FName identity. Local/inherited collisions,
descendant collisions (including keys introduced by a new parent), parent cycles,
missing/incompatible key classes, inherited-key mutations and native persistent
SelfActor mutations are rejected before changes. Parent chains are bounded to
32, effective keys to 1024 or the lower native ID capacity, and Blackboard and
Behavior Tree dependency discovery to 512 assets per family. Native AI settings
manage adding/removing SelfActor on parent changes. UE's native field is
`bInstanceSynced`; this shares values between Blackboard instances and is not an
instance-editable flag. Category and description limits are 128/4096 characters.

Structural edits report referencer packages in dry-run and require confirmation
when referencers exist. Rename updates direct FBlackboardKeySelector properties
in related Behavior Tree packages, including trees using descendant Blackboards,
and resolves their native cached keys. Save includes only trees with selectors
changed by this rename. Other structural edits can leave external selectors
requiring repair; arbitrary Blueprint/string references and nested/container
selector adapters are separate work. Key-type replacement uses fresh native
defaults unless typed settings are supplied in the same request; supported native
key settings and their verification are described below.
A weak tracked cache and module-owned undo/redo hook refresh native hierarchy IDs
and synchronization state after serialized changes without retaining assets.

The UE 5.7 editor target built successfully. Native automation
`UE5MCP.Blackboard.SelectorRenameUndo` passed with a real MoveTo task selector:
preview preservation, referencer confirmation, rename, resolved native ID, undo
and redo. The REST fixture passed metadata/type/rename/parent authoring, local and
inherited collision/cycle/ownership guards, rejected-request preservation,
descendant ID updates after deletion and undo, synchronization propagation and
undo/redo, native SelfActor parent transitions, dependency preview/confirmation,
dry-run/no-op and PIE guards. A fresh editor passed saved hierarchy, local and
inherited IDs, metadata, replacement type, synchronization flags and clean package
state. Owned fixtures were removed. Cold persistence of external selector
rewrites, Struct/custom/deprecated key defaults, broader Blackboard-provider references and
Behavior Tree graph/runtime compatibility remain separate gates.

### Blackboard Native Key Settings

Key add/update requests now accept `bSetTypeSettings=true` with a typed
`TypeSettings` object. Exact native Bool, Int, Float, Name, String, Vector,
Rotator, Object, Class and Enum keys are supported. Inspection reports each
local/inherited key's `type_settings`, support status, stored default, applicable
constraints/flags and settings errors. The top-level validation keeps a separate
`structurally_valid` flag and includes supported settings errors in `valid`.
Custom, Struct and deprecated native-enum key settings are explicitly separate.

`bSetDefault` selects the corresponding typed field: BoolValue, IntValue,
FloatValue, TextValue, VectorValue, RotationValue or ReferenceValue. Int values
must fit int32; Float defaults are finite within +/-1e30, Name/String defaults
are limited to 128/4096 UTF-16 code units, and Vector/Rotator components are finite
within +/-1e9 (rotation in degrees). Vector/Rotator store their value separately
from `bSetUseDefault/bUseDefault`; setting a value does not implicitly enable
initialization from it. Disabled defaults retain the native invalid/unset value
at runtime.

Object/Class keys accept `bSetBaseClass/BaseClass`. Object defaults require an
existing persistent asset or native class compatible with the base; Class
defaults must derive from the base. Empty ReferenceValue explicitly clears the
default. World actors, subobject paths and class-default objects are rejected as
Object defaults. Enum configuration uses `bSetEnumType/EnumTypePath` and optional
`bSetNativeEnumName/NativeEnumName`: nonempty native overrides require a full
/Script enum path, and an empty override restores ordinary EnumType selection.
Enum members must fit the native unsigned byte excluding generated MAX, and
numeric defaults must name a member or a native-valid flag combination. Enum
member validation is bounded to 1024 and occurs before native editor handlers,
avoiding invalid-enum modal dialogs. Existing native-name overrides must be
explicitly cleared when switching to an ordinary EnumType.

The full prospective key settings are validated on a transient duplicate before
metadata/type/default changes. Existing owned key objects are transacted in place;
class changes create fresh owned native key objects and apply requested settings
in the same transaction. Dry-run/no-op, class-default isolation, save and existing
PIE guards apply. Base-class/Enum-type changes use the existing referencer
confirmation rule. They do not rewrite arbitrary external selector constraints.

The UE 5.7 target built. Native automation `UE5MCP.Blackboard.NativeDefaults`
initialized real UBlackboardComponents in an owned transient Game world with its
native AI system and read all ten supported value types through native GetValue.
It also verified unset Vector/Rotator values, String key-instance isolation,
class-default preservation, native Enum-name set/clear, default undo/redo, and
mixed-request rejection for a signed out-of-byte-range Enum, and safe rejection
of a malformed local key with no type object. The final rebuild and native
regression passed and the owned test editor exited with status 0. The MoveTo selector
rename/undo/redo regression passed. The REST fixture passed typed creation and
replacement, defaults/constraints/Enum inspection, preflight/no-op/dry-run,
invalid bounds/reference/class/Enum rejection without partial metadata changes,
existing-subobject undo/redo, inherited settings, reference clearing and
referencer confirmation. A fresh editor passed saved native defaults, Object/Class
constraints, Enum type/name validity and inherited settings with clean packages.
Owned fixtures were removed. User-defined Enum persistence, Struct/custom key
settings, Blueprint generated-class constraints and live updates of already
initialized Blackboard instances require separate gates; editing assets during
PIE remains rejected.

## Data Asset and Data Registry Coverage Audit

`UDataTable` row operations are implemented. Generic asset property
inspection/editing is implemented, but there is no dedicated support for
`UDataAsset`, `UPrimaryDataAsset`, typed data-asset creation, primary asset
metadata, or Data Registry editing.

Add:

- Data Asset class discovery and safe creation from a selected native or
  Blueprint data-asset class.
- Typed property get/set with class compatibility validation, nested structs,
  arrays, sets, maps, soft references, and asset references.
- Primary asset ID, bundle, chunk, and management metadata inspection/editing.
- Data Registry source/configuration inspection, row lookup, import/refresh,
  and validation where public APIs permit mutation.
- Dedicated `/data-assets/*`, `/primary-assets/*`, and `/data-registries/*`
  route families with dry-run, save, dirty-state, and validation responses.

## Audio Asset Coverage Audit

Initial audio routes inspect Sound Wave, Sound Cue, Sound Class, Sound Mix, and
Sound Submix assets, edit reflected settings, and provide class-level validation.
Sound Attenuation assets can now be created, inspected, validated, and edited
through reflected audio properties; audio sections can assign and inspect an
attenuation asset reference.
Sound Concurrency assets can now be created and inspected, and use the shared
audio settings and validation routes for their reflected voice-management
settings.
Sound Wave routes now report imported duration, channels, sample rate, and
source-file status. Guarded native audio import, replacement, and reimport support
dry-run, explicit confirmation, and save controls. A disposable live fixture
passed import, duplicate rejection, confirmed replacement, same-file reimport,
and confirmed source-path change. Typed `/audio/waves/settings` now reads and
edits compression type and quality, sample-rate quality, looping, loading
behavior, cloud streaming, Sound Class, attenuation, and concurrency
references with dry-run/save controls. `/audio/waves/validate` checks codec,
quality, playback values, and imported metadata; `/audio/waves/rebuild` forces
and waits for platform audio data. A disposable imported WAV passed settings
preflight/readback, invalid-quality rejection, validation, rebuild, save, and
cleanup. More complete audio authoring remains:

`/sound-cues/create`, `/sound-cues/graph`, and `/sound-cues/validate` now create
Sound Cue assets, inspect graph IDs, node settings, positions, pins and links,
and add/remove nodes, connect/disconnect pins, edit node settings, move/layout
nodes, compile and validate the graph. Wave Player nodes use typed Sound Wave
references; other node settings use validated reflected properties. Node
deletion requires confirmation, and graph edits support dry-run and save. A
disposable Cue with a Wave Player and Modulator passed node/property/connection
edits, link validation, confirmed deletion and cleanup. A two-session test also
verified the Wave reference, Modulator setting and root links after editor
restart.

MetaSound support is implemented under `/metasounds`: create source and patch
assets, optionally as presets from a same-type parent, discover registered
referenceable node classes, inspect interfaces/nodes/defaults/locations/edges,
and add/remove/connect/disconnect/move nodes. Removing a node requires explicit
confirmation; input defaults support Float, Int32, Bool, and String literals.
Graph edits support dry-run and save. Validation checks frontend-document
validity and edge endpoints/pins/types/cardinality; compile registers the graph
with the MetaSound frontend and reports validity and save state. A live test
connected a SuperOscillator output to a source Audio output, set Frequency to
440, compiled and saved the graph, created a source preset from it, restarted
the editor, and verified the source graph and preset survived. A separate live
check created and compiled a patch, created a same-type patch preset, and
verified its preset flag. Temporary test assets were deleted after verification.

Typed `/sound-classes/settings`, `/sound-mixes/settings`, and
`/sound-submixes/settings` inspect and edit Sound Class gain, pitch, filter,
routing, loading behavior, parent, and default-submix references; Sound Mix
timing, four EQ bands, and per-class volume/pitch/filter/center-channel
adjusters; and Sound Submix parent, auto-disable, envelope follower, dB levels,
and effect-chain presets. Dedicated validation routes check numeric bounds,
class/submix hierarchy consistency, Sound Mix adjuster/EQ data, and passive
activation cycles. Parent cycles are rejected; removing Sound Mix adjusters or
Submix effects requires confirmation. Disposable copies of Engine Sound Class,
Sound Mix, and Sound Submix assets passed dry-run, editing, validation, save,
reload readback, confirmed removal, and cleanup tests.

`/audio/waves/import-formats` reports extensions advertised by the installed
native Sound Factory. UE 5.7 Win64 supports WAV, AIF, AIFF, FLAC, Ogg Vorbis,
Opus, and MP3. Non-WAV sources are decoded during preflight, including dry-run;
unsupported extensions and malformed sources are rejected before asset edits.
Confirmed reimports use the native factory explicitly, preserving the existing
Sound Wave object and settings while supporting AIFF and cross-format source
changes without import dialogs. Source inspection reports stored import duration
separately from looping playback duration. A stereo fixture matrix passed
import, same-file reimport, dry-run, confirmed cross-format changes, settings
preservation, save/reload, and cleanup for every advertised extension. The
existing WAV replacement/reimport regression also passed. Decoder buffers are
shrunk before preflight to avoid the UE 5.7 memory reader's allocation-size EOF
boundary assertion discovered by the Ogg test.

`/audio/attenuations/settings` now exposes validated numeric, boolean, and enum
controls for distance falloff and shape geometry, spatialization, air absorption,
listener focus, occlusion, reverb sends, and priority attenuation. Inspection
returns the accepted setting names and enum choices. Edits preflight the entire
proposed settings struct, including related distance ranges and shape geometry,
before mutation; dry-run preserves the asset and dirty state.
`/audio/attenuations/curves` assigns an external Curve Float reference or replaces
and clears inline normalized curves for distance volume, low/high-pass
absorption, reverb, and priority. Existing curve replacement/clearing requires
confirmation, and external curve assets are never edited by this adapter.
`/audio/attenuations/validate` checks settings and curve keys.
`/audio/attenuations/evaluate` samples native distance-volume gain at 1-256 world
positions using an origin, rotation, and distance scale; its scope excludes
runtime occlusion tracing, filtering, and actual audio rendering. Disposable
assets passed numeric/enum/geometry rejection without mutation, dry-run,
sphere/box/capsule/cone sampling including a transformed cone, custom curves,
all three interpolation modes, confirmed replacement/clear, external references,
save/reload, and cleanup.

Attenuation routing progress: `/audio/attenuations/submix-sends` now upserts,
removes, and clears up to 64 destination sends with Manual, Linear, or CustomCurve
control. It supports manual unclamped amplification, level/distance ranges,
inline curve keys, and external Curve Float references. Native clamping of
external send curves is reported in validation when keys exceed 0-1.
`/audio/attenuations/plugins` adds/removes/clears compatible spatialization,
occlusion, reverb, and source-data-override settings references.
`/audio/plugin-settings/classes` lists loaded concrete settings classes, and
`/audio/plugin-settings/create` creates default settings assets from those
compatible classes. Inspection exposes all routing references; settings edits
also support send-enable flags and an optional AudioLink settings override.
Dry-run preserves assets, and removal/clear or destructive curve replacement
requires confirmation. The validator checks destination/reference validity,
duplicates, enum values, ranges, and custom send curves. Referenced settings,
submixes, and curves are not mutated by link editing; plugin-specific parameter
editing continues through shared reflected property tools. A live test with
Spatialization enabled only for the test editor sessions passed three send
methods, curve/reference edits, incompatible-class rejection, default plugin
settings creation, confirmation guards, save/reload, source dirty-state
preservation, and cleanup. Core attenuation regression tests also passed.

Dialogue authoring is implemented under `/audio/dialogue`: native Voice/Wave
factories create assets; voice settings edit grammatical gender/plurality while
preserving localization GUIDs; wave settings edit spoken text, subtitle override,
voice direction, and the mature flag. Context upsert/remove/clear operations
validate voice and recorded Sound Wave references, target uniqueness, native
context-hash uniqueness, and localization-key format/uniqueness before mutation.
The initial empty factory context is reused for the first authored mapping.
Existing contexts can be selected by their native hash ID or by exact speaker
and ordered targets; speaker/target replacement returns the new context ID.
Native `UpdateContext` refreshes cached proxies after metadata or mapping edits.
Resolution reports native context support, proxy playability, localized text,
localization keys, and recorded-audio filenames without starting playback.
Validation distinguishes structurally valid drafts from contexts ready for
playback. Removal/clear requires confirmation; edits support dry-run and save.
A disposable fixture passed factory creation, enum/class/duplicate-key
rejection, metadata and context edits, subtitle fallback/override, GUID and
context-ID persistence, native resolution, speaker/target replacement,
procedural MetaSound rejection, confirmed removal/clear, save/reload, referenced
audio dirty-state preservation, and cleanup.

Quartz runtime control is implemented under `/audio/quartz/clock` (inspection)
and `/audio/quartz/control` (create/time_signature/tempo/start/pause/resume/stop/reset/delete).
These routes select a native PIE world; an explicit PIE instance is required
when multiple worlds are available. The normal editor world has no Quartz
subsystem, so an active play session is required. Creation validates BPM and
time signature and chooses either the audio engine or subsystem clock manager.
Controls queue native proxy commands on the owning clock thread; inspection
reports existence, running state, BPM, cached transport/runtime, and fixed note
durations. Reset/stop reapply the unchanged tick rate to refresh paused native
transport caches. Native timestamp `seconds` can retain its historical value
after paused reset; use runtime and bar/beat counters to observe reset.
UE 5.7's public Bar/Beat duration getter ignores the configured meter, so those
two values are deliberately omitted and the response explains the limitation.
Clock creation rejects existing names, deletion requires confirmation, and all
controls support dry-run. Clocks are runtime objects and are never saved as
assets. A live PIE smoke test passed both native managers, 3/8 transport, tempo
changes, fixed note timing, pause/resume/reset/stop, validation, dry-run,
confirmed deletion, and cleanup.
Creation and `time_signature` now accept pulse override groups using native
fixed-note quantizations. Groups require positive counts, at most 32 groups/
128 pulses, and a total duration matching exactly one requested bar. Dependent
Bar/Beat values, None/Count, under-filled/over-filled bars and invalid counts are
rejected before queuing. An empty override list restores ordinary meter beats.
Dynamic signature changes reset native transport before changing the meter,
preserving running/paused state and clearing UE 5.7's old pulse cursor safely.
Responses report requested meter/group settings and reset submission; they do
not present the request as a native settings readback, since no public
time-signature getter exists. A native PIE test passed 7/8 grouped 2+2+3 timing,
running pulse-array shortening to grouped 5/8, ordinary 5/4 meter, override
clearing, reset behavior, dry-run and invalid-input rejection with both clock
managers. The prior lifecycle/tempo/reset regression also passed.
`/audio/quartz/events` schedules native quantized tempo changes, transport
resets, notifications and synchronized starts of another clock; it also
subscribes/unsubscribes to native metronome divisions and cancels/releases
requests. Each ID owns a native clock handle and game-thread observer, bounded
to 128 IDs per PIE world and 256 retained events per ID. Musical division,
multiplier, counting reference, clock references and BPM are validated before
submission. Boundary controls include fire-on-start, cancel-if-not-running and
resume-on-queue. Cross-manager other-clock starts produce an explicit adapter
rejection before entering native command execution. Individual cancellation
uses the public native pending-command API. Native queued/about-to-start/
started/canceled/failure callbacks and metronome payloads are polled using a
sequence cursor; responses expose oldest/latest/next sequence and dropped-event
counts. Receipt times are monotonic game-thread delivery times, not audio-frame
execution timestamps. Native command names and metronome bar/beat fields are
preserved. Subscription close stops recording late callbacks. Pending requests
must reach a terminal callback before release while their clock exists.
World teardown/module shutdown release observers and subscriptions; weak
command ownership avoids retaining deleted clocks through cancellation queues.
A native PIE test passed tempo/reset/notify/start-other execution and callbacks,
individual cancellation, subscriptions, cursor pagination/overflow, dry-run,
invalid-request rejection, paused-clock cancellation, resume-on-queue,
cross-manager rejection and pending/subscription teardown with both clock
managers. The existing Quartz lifecycle regression also passed.
Quantized playback now uses native `UAudioComponent::PlayQuantized` through
`play_sound`, with stop/pause/resume controls and owned transient PIE
components. SoundBase references, audio engine clock ownership, start offset,
fade duration, volume and pitch ranges are preflight validated. Dry-run creates
no observer or component. Inspection exposes native registration/play state and
source/settings; native command callbacks establish boundary execution, while
`OnAudioFinished` reports completion (including explicit stops). Command terminal
state is separate from sound completion, and native IsPlaying may include queued
audio before its boundary. Stop uses the native component API, including its
anticipatory queue cancellation behavior; release stops and destroys the component
even when pending. World/module cleanup also destroys owned components.
A native PIE test passed delayed start/finish callbacks, pause/resume, queued and
active stop, pending release, validation, dry-run and PIE cleanup.
Playback optionally enables spatialization and accepts world location/rotation,
native Sound Attenuation/Concurrency references, and attachment to a registered
scene component in the selected PIE world. Source/attenuation settings determine
effective spatialization; the flag permits native spatialization rather than
overriding source rendering rules. Default playback keeps the previous nonspatial
UI sound behavior. Transform validation bounds finite positions/angles before
component creation or movement. Attachment rejects editor/other-world components,
unregistered components and invalid sockets. `move_sound` updates world transform
while retaining attachment. Inspection reads native world transforms, component
path, attachment/socket, spatial/UI flags, attenuation settings and concurrency
references. A live test passed native spatial start, transform/attachment readback,
movement/dry-run, parent release with world-transform preservation, malformed
references/transforms/socket and editor-world rejection, and unchanged attenuation/
concurrency asset settings after playback.
`/audio/components/settings` now inspects and edits Blueprint SCS/native default-subobject
Audio Component templates. It supports typed gain, pitch, low/high-pass filter,
priority/subtitle settings, serializable playback flags, Sound/Attenuation/Class
references and bounded concurrency sets. References are type checked and all
requested values are validated before transaction/mutation. Empty reference paths
clear native references; explicit concurrency replacement supports clearing.
Dry-run leaves settings/dirty state unchanged; no-op edits avoid transactions and
compilation. Real changes use an editor transaction and compile the Blueprint;
optional save persists its native package. PIE blocks real edits/saves. Native
default-subobject edits target the selected Blueprint's own CDO; existing
Blueprint component creation/attachment routes compose with this settings API.
A disposable Blueprint test passed validation atomicity, dry-run/no-op, undo/redo,
compile/save, PIE rejection, cold editor restart readback and reference/set clearing.
The same route accepts an exclusive `ActorPath` instead of `BpPath` for persistent
Audio Component instances in the current editor world. Actor-owned and
Blueprint-created instances are edited independently of their archetypes. Current
editor-world identity, native component type and persistence flags are validated;
PIE/runtime objects and ambiguous target paths are rejected. Actor and component
participate in the native transaction and post-edit workflow. Inspection/mutation
responses expose the owning package path/dirty state. Optional save writes that
map/external actor package through native package saving, including other changes
in the same package; new maps/actor packages require the world save workflow first.
A disposable nonpartitioned map test passed native/Blueprint-created instance
editing, atomic validation, dry-run/no-op, undo/redo, package save, cold editor
restart readback and archetype independence. The Blueprint template persistence
regression also passed against the extended API.
Inherited Blueprint SCS components now resolve their effective native template
through the owning class hierarchy and respect editable-when-inherited. Inspection
exposes the defining Blueprint, inherited state and local override existence;
inspection/dry-run/no-op do not allocate override records. Real child edits create
native `UInheritableComponentHandler` overrides inside the transaction and leave
the ancestor's node/template unchanged. `bResetInheritedOverride` removes the
child's native override record and restores inheritance; it cannot be combined
with other settings. Native property-inheritance queries identify descendant
templates/instances that inherit each supported setting, so parent changes and
reset propagate numeric, boolean, reference and concurrency values without
overwriting customized properties. Affected descendants participate in the
transaction and are marked dirty; optional save applies only to the requested
Blueprint, so other affected packages still require saving. Advanced component
properties outside this typed settings API remain outside its propagation scope.
A native multilevel Blueprint test passed inherited inspection without allocation,
dry-run/no-op and rejected-reference atomicity, ancestor/sibling isolation,
transaction undo/redo, numeric/boolean/reference/concurrency propagation with
customized values preserved, reset and descendant propagation, save and cold
editor restart readback. Template and placed-instance persistence regressions
also passed against the final build.
Native C++ Audio Component default subobjects are resolved from the selected
Blueprint's own actor CDO, with default-subobject, direct ownership and package
identity checks. Edits use that Blueprint-owned component and participate in
compile/save/undo and supported-property descendant propagation. Inspection
reports the native-template scope, immediate archetype and whether supported
settings differ from that archetype. Reset restores supported settings from the
immediate parent archetype; SCS overrides continue to use native handler records.
A disposable AmbientSound Blueprint hierarchy passed dry-run/no-op, invalid-input
atomicity, multilevel numeric/boolean/reference/concurrency propagation, undo/reset,
independent native-derived Blueprint isolation, save and cold editor restart.
Actors spawned after restart received the saved component settings. The SCS
inheritance regression also passed against the same build.
World Partition external-actor persistence is now verified with a disposable map
created from the installed Open World template. Actor-owned and Blueprint-created
components used their actual external actor packages; saves changed those files
while leaving the map file hash unchanged. Dry-run, invalid-input atomicity,
undo/redo, no-op/save, stable package identity, cold editor restart and Blueprint
default independence passed. The fixture uses always-loaded actors so the tested
components are available after map load. Cleanup removes its uniquely named map,
Blueprint, generated HLOD assets and guarded external actor/object directories.
Further audio diagnostics and advanced component properties outside the supported
typed settings/propagation scope remain pending.

Modulation authoring is implemented under `/audio/modulation`: create native
parameter, Control Bus, and Control Bus Mix assets; inspect/edit typed settings;
convert bounded batches using the native parameter conversion functions;
upsert/remove/clear mix stages; and validate domains, references and timing.
Supported parameter types are scalar, scaled, frequency, filter frequency,
volume, bipolar and additive. Edits validate complete proposed state in a
transient preview before a transaction; numeric fields are limited to the
selected parameter class. Unit display caches are refreshed through the native
API and are excluded from no-op change detection. Buses support parameter
references, bypass, address overrides and compatible generator references;
removing generator links requires confirmation. Mix stages use unique bus
references, normalized targets and attack/release times; removal/clear requires
confirmation. Mutations support dry-run and save. The plugin explicitly depends
on AudioModulation, and shared audio inspection/validation includes these assets.
A two-session live test passed all seven parameter classes, linear/logarithmic/
bipolar conversions, bounds and class rejection, dry-run state preservation,
bus references/address/bypass edits, two mix stages with native unit readback,
duration/retrigger settings, save/reload, no-op dirty-state preservation,
confirmed stage removal/clear, bus-link clearing and fixture cleanup.

Modulation creation also supports patches, native LFO/AD envelope/envelope
follower generators, and Audio Bus source assets. The common inspector and
validator cover their settings and references. `/audio/modulation/generators/settings`
edits class-specific numeric fields, bypass/loop/invert flags, LFO shape and
envelope follower Audio Bus references. Audio Bus channel counts use the native
1/2/4/6/8-channel configurations. Patch settings edit the output parameter and
bypass flag; patches start as native bypassed drafts. `/audio/modulation/inputs`
upserts/removes/clears unique Control Bus inputs, sample-and-hold flags and
transforms. Built-in WaveTable curves, custom normalized Linear/Constant/Cubic
keys and shared Curve Float references are supported. File-driven transforms
use the guarded import workflow described below. Removal/clear requires confirmation; edits validate
complete proposed state and support transactions, dry-run and save.
`/audio/modulation/sample` uses a fresh native LFO/AD instance for bounded
sampling or applies the native transform to bounded patch input values. It
does not sample live playback state or simulate patch mixing, output conversion,
sample-and-hold state, or envelope follower audio input. The follower inspector
reports whether an Audio Bus source is assigned; live sampling is available
through the recording workflow below. Typed validation propagates known generator errors
through bus/patch references while preserving references to compatible custom
generator classes handled by shared property tools.
A two-session live test passed all three generator classes, LFO/AD native
sampling, Audio Bus channel/follower source edits, positive generator links,
built-in/custom/shared transforms, curve sampling, dry-run and invalid-request
rejection, save/reload and clean no-op edits, confirmed generator/input removal,
source clearing, referenced-asset dirty-state preservation and cleanup. The
existing parameter/bus/mix save/reload regression passed alongside this fixture.

`/audio/modulation/inputs/import` imports/reimports file-driven patch inputs
using transient native Sound Factory imports and the native WaveTable importer.
It accepts the factory's WAV/AIF/AIFF/FLAC/Ogg/Opus/MP3 formats, absolute local
paths, bounded source data, channel selection (with native channel wrapping),
16-4096 power-of-two resolution, IEEE float/PCM16 processed tables, phase,
trim, fades, normalization and offset removal. Preflight decodes and processes
the source during dry-run, checks finite samples and complete sample frames,
rejects malformed sources and invalid edits, and requires confirmation for
replacement/reimport. Reimport defaults to the stored source and edit settings.
Changed asset saves during PIE are rejected before mutation.
UE 5.7's cached-table `FWaveTableTransform::Apply` mis-scales normalized indices
and assumes float table data. Playback therefore uses an owned native Shared
Curve Float baked from the processed table. The complete native file transform,
including imported PCM source samples, is serialized into editor metadata for
inspection and reimport. Inspection reports the actual Shared runtime curve
and its file-source recipe explicitly. Each changed recipe creates an immutable
owned curve so undo/redo restores matching source metadata. Native fade-out
ratios at exact sample boundaries are adjusted slightly to avoid the importer's
endpoint overrun; responses preserve precision for the effective stored value.
Preflight copies and their owned subobjects are fully transient; patch settings
preflight preserves original input references and source recipes.
A two-session fixture passed all seven formats, native channel/resolution/edit
processing, IEEE float/PCM16 table recipes, source replacement, invalid/NaN
source rejection, dry-run, no-op reimport, live PIE playback/curve parity,
undo/redo, save/reload, cached sampling after source removal, curve replacement
and cleanup. Existing parameter/bus/mix and generator/patch fixtures passed
save/reload regression after the shared transient-copy change.

`/audio/modulation/runtime` now controls native PIE modulation destinations,
mix activation/deactivation, runtime stage overrides, restore from asset,
modulator updates and global bus values. Destinations hold buses/generators/
patches active through UE 5.7's current destination API. Inspection reports
native values and mix activity plus the adapter-owned destination list; it
does not claim to list all engine destinations or infer activity from a value.
Commands are asynchronous and runtime-only, with dry-run and typed validation.
Runtime mix stage updates require an active mix and unique buses already in
its asset definition. Owned destinations, mix references and global values
are cleaned up on world teardown and module shutdown. A live two-PIE-session
test passed bus/patch values, live LFO changes, mix/global value edits, dry-run,
invalid-request rejection, unchanged saved asset state and teardown cleanup.

Runtime filtering now uses native `UpdateMixByFilter` with optional bus address,
exact parameter class and parameter asset filters. The active native mix proxy
performs matching; responses report requested filters and never infer a matched
count from saved assets. Empty address patterns match all native stages. Patterns
are bounded and validated before queuing, including paired/nonempty groups to
avoid native matcher assertions. UE 5.7's native `PartsMatch` has prefix semantics,
and terminal brace alternatives can return no matches; character classes such as
`[AB]` work for single-character alternatives. The adapter preserves these native
semantics and documents the limitation.
Batch operations activate/deactivate mixes, refresh active mixes from assets,
refresh modulators and set/clear shared-target global bus values. They accept
1-128 unique typed asset paths, validate every asset/activity requirement before
submitting anything and enforce the combined per-world ownership limits. Native
commands then process independently without a rollback guarantee. Dry-run queues
nothing. Explicit `clear_all_globals` and `deactivate_all_mixes` use the native
device-wide APIs, including state created outside this adapter; responses expose
that scope and adapter ownership tracking is cleared accordingly.
A live PIE test passed address wildcards/character classes, exact parameter class
and asset intersections, empty/no-match filters, the native terminal-brace behavior,
malformed-pattern rejection, batch validation without partial activation/refresh/
global edits, dry-run, mix restoration, modulator refresh submission with live LFO
values, global batches, device-wide resets, unchanged asset settings and teardown
cleanup. The prior modulation runtime regression also passed.

`/audio/modulation/recordings` starts/stops/releases bounded recordings from native
PIE modulation destinations. It holds the selected modulator active until the
recording completes/stops, then retains readings until release or world cleanup.
Envelope followers require an assigned Audio Bus. Per-world limits are 16 retained
recordings and 1024 readings per recording; interval/duration requests are bounded
and preflight checked. Polling uses sequence cursors and reports running/stop state.
Values come directly from native destination `GetValue` on the core game-thread
ticker, with monotonic receipt times. These are latest modulation-tick readings,
not sample-accurate PCM/cooked envelope analysis; initial/inactive fallback can be
1, and missed ticker intervals are never synthesized. Asset/bus paths capture the
source configuration at recording start. World cleanup/module shutdown release
native destinations and buffers; stopped/completed recordings release activity
while keeping their data available.
Owned Quartz sound components now accept validated pre/post-effect Audio Bus
sends during play or via `set_audio_bus_sends`. Up to 16 unique bus/stage pairs
are retained per component; levels are bounded to [0,4], zero mutes a route, and
the source SoundBase must enable bus sends. Entire updates validate before native
setters run. The observer retains bus references for component lifetime, and
inspection labels route levels as requested settings rather than mixer readback.
A native rendered-audio test passed silence/tone/silence follower rise and decay,
live bus-send mute/restore, cursor paging, stop/release, malformed requests,
dry-run, retained-recording limits, unchanged source assets and two-PIE teardown
cleanup. Existing quantized playback and modulation runtime regressions passed.

`/audio/diagnostics/captures` queues bounded native audio-thread snapshots and
polls/releases them by ID. It reads `FAudioDevice::GetActiveSounds` on its owning
audio thread, filters rows by native world ID and weak world identity, and reports
device-wide/world logical active-sound counts. Rows include native instance and
component IDs, playback/unscaled time, raw volume/pitch multipliers, pause/UI flags
and historical virtualization state. Device configuration is captured on the same
audio thread. Completed numeric data stays frozen; weak sound/component paths are
resolved on the game thread at inspection and can become empty after destruction.
Limits are 1-512 retained rows, 16 captures per world and 128 global retained/pending
entries. Full logical counts remain available when rows are truncated. Dry-run
does not queue a capture. Pending releases/world cleanup retain a game-thread-owned
device handle until native work publishes completion; no game-thread callback is
queued from the audio command. Module shutdown drains the audio command fence
before releasing handles and unloading code. These snapshots cover logical active
sounds and configuration, not separate virtual-loop lists, hardware voice counts,
PCM, or CPU/DSP trace profiling.
A native PIE test passed real playback/source identity, raw settings, advancing
playback time, immutable completed captures, pause/resume/stop, destroyed-component
path resolution, row truncation/full counts, dry-run, invalid inputs, resource caps,
release and two-PIE cleanup. Native logs confirmed audio-device teardown, and the
rendered-audio envelope-follower regression passed alongside the capture workflow.

`/audio/profiling/traces` starts, polls, stops and releases process-wide native
Unreal trace files through `FTraceAuxiliary`. Channel discovery exposes availability,
enabled state and read-only state for audio, audiomixer, cpu, frame and bookmark.
Start requires a selected PIE world, a unique ID and no existing native connection
or paused session. Files stay under Saved/Profiling/UE5MCP; existing files are never
overwritten, and releasing metadata preserves the file for Unreal Insights.
Only channels enabled by this capture are restored after native connection close.
Native connection callbacks establish trace GUID ownership before control; a
replaced connection is left untouched. One active trace and 16 retained records
are allowed. Duration is bounded to 0.1-60 seconds and the soft file-size stop
threshold to 1-256 MiB; native buffering/asynchronous closure can overshoot it.
Manual stop, duration expiry and selected-world cleanup request native shutdown.
Dry-run validates without enabling channels, starting a trace or creating a record.
A native PIE test passed actual Quartz playback, channel enablement/restoration,
file growth, native file-header/session GUID identity, manual/duration/world-cleanup
completion, file retention, no overwrite, malformed requests and dry-run. A separate
editor started with a command-line trace passed refusal of adapter start/stop
requests while preserving that independent session through PIE teardown. These
tests verify capture and file identity, not decoded audio event counts. In-app
trace analysis, hardware-voice summaries and CPU/DSP attribution remain pending.

`/audio/modulation/profiles` inspects native on-disk profiles and submits native
save/load operations. Profile indices are bounded to 0-999; paths follow UE
5.7's native serializer under the project's Saved/Config/AudioModulation tree.
Native saves capture inactive asset settings or active proxy stage state and
complete asynchronously; inspection reads the resulting file. Native profiles
store stage target/attack/release only, excluding mix duration/retrigger.
Loading validates the on-disk size, stage count, bus classes and numeric domains
before priming the native ini cache and invoking the native loader. The returned
full stage list is used for confirmed asset import, supporting added/removed
membership beyond the native loader's matching-stage update. Changed imports
use an editor transaction and optional save; no-op imports preserve asset
dirty state while still restoring an active runtime mix. Profile overwrite and
changed asset import require confirmation; dry-run preserves files and assets.
Audio context selects an active PIE world or the editor's main audio device.
Changed asset saves during PIE are rejected before mutation; stop PIE before
saving imported stages. A two-session fixture passed native inactive/active
saves, overwrite/confirmation guards, malformed-profile rejection, stage
membership import, asset save/reload and profile persistence, no-op runtime
restoration, clean dirty state, the PIE save guard and cleanup.

Remaining audio support:

- Further Quartz scheduling/event/settings extensions described above.
  Sound Concurrency has creation, inspection, and shared reflected
  settings/validation. Plugin-specific typed parameter adapters remain beyond
  the implemented compatible reference management and shared property tools.
- Custom generator adapters, hardware-voice summaries and native trace analysis
  with CPU/DSP attribution beyond the implemented Unreal Insights file capture.

Proposed route families include `/audio/waves/*`, `/audio/concurrencies/*`,
`/sound-cues/*`, `/metasounds/*`, `/sound-classes/*`, `/sound-mixes/*`,
`/sound-submixes/*`, and `/audio/validate`.

## Texture Coverage Audit

Texture support is currently partial, not absent. Implemented routes cover
inspection, reflected settings, platform settings, refresh, resource rebuild,
validation, source-file diagnostics, and guarded local-image import, replacement,
and reimport for loadable texture assets. The import routes validate a local
source path, require explicit confirmation for replacement or reimport, and
support dry-run and save controls.

Source-only continuation now implements dedicated 2D/cube/volume/2D-array
render-target discovery, inspection, native-factory creation, typed settings,
dimension authoring, clear-color authoring and optional full native snapshots.
These adapters are uncompiled and runtime/undo/persistence unverified; all new
verification remains deferred in UNTESTED_FEATURES.md. Dedicated conversion now inspects native format policy and creates or updates
source-backed counterpart textures using native GPU readback with full snapshots.
Readback does not prove capture freshness/pixel quality. Source-only export now covers native target DDS and selected-slice PNG/EXR/HDR, plus source-backed DDS mip chains and selected source mip-slice PNG/EXR/HDR. All export adapters remain uncompiled/output unverified. Larger/custom-format target
mutations and explicit derived-data/pixel workflows remain open.

Source-backed continuation implements native-factory Texture2D creation without
an image file, volume creation with optional2D source, and2D/cube-array creation
from loaded source textures. Array adapters inspect/discover sources, diagnose
source-header policy, and replace/reorder native source lists. Volume adapters
inspect/discover sources, edit address/tile layout, and reassign sources. Cube
textures have source-header/authored-field inspection and loaded discovery.

Dedicated Texture2D settings now cover address/filter/mip generation and load
policy/LOD limits/processing flags/color adjustments/padding mode-color/paired
build resize with exact current/source-ID and optional authored snapshots.
Source block/layer/mip/identity metadata and cached streaming state are exposed.
Explicit source decode supports BGRA8 pixel pages/statistics/comparison, guarded
source-mip fill/patch/copy and native mip-chain decode-size validation with decoded
payload SHA1 fingerprints. Native2D/cube/volume/2D-array/cube-array creation supports
source-file-free dimensions and RGBA fill, with native callback/registry handling.
VT authored policy inspection and prefetch/priority edits preserve streaming mode.
Native duplication retains external references/import source paths; direct loaded
material-instance overrides, texture-base expressions (with authored sampler
policy diagnostics), and SlateBrushAsset references can be inspected.

RuntimeVirtualTexture now has native asset inspect/discovery/create/duplicate,
layer policy and mandatory snapshot-guarded authored settings. Components expose
full settings, platform override pages, native asset/builder references, soft
bounds-actor assignment, boolean/numeric/enum/fixed-color/per-platform authoring.
Primitive writer lists/LOD-culling/main-pass authoring and discovery are available.
Native volumes support guarded create/delete/world-transform authoring. Direct
component/primitive/sample-expression/material-instance consumers are exposed.
Adaptive toggles reject tile-count truncation; native callbacks can recreate
producers/resources, and no rendered/page residency result is proven.

Streaming runtime-VT builder containers have native inspection/discovery/empty
factory creation, direct component consumer pages and guarded separate-mobile
policy. Embedded desktop/mobile refs and client hash metadata are exposed;
container creation does not generate data and hash freshness is not validated.
A guarded native BuildAllStreamedMips adapter and explicit native streaming
status checks now exist in source, with documented compilation/render waits,
feature-level changes and partial failure. Native bounds alignment, sample
reference-policy synchronization and instance override CRUD/effective lookup
also exist; none has been executed or verified in this continuation.

All continuation adapters remain uncompiled/runtime/undo/persistence unverified.
Remaining dedicated workflows include:

- Broader cube/source-free subtype creation, conversion/import/export and
  generated/platform/derived texture-specific authoring beyond listed adapters.
- Actual source pixel integrity/decode validation and generated mip editing,
  derived-data freshness/status, complete per-platform policy authoring,
  compression preview/statistics and virtual-page residency diagnostics.
- VT mode conversion with material sampler migration/compatibility, runtime
  virtual-texture family workflows, and platform/project compatibility proof.
- Full material/UI reference validation beyond loaded direct authored overrides,
  expression defaults and brush assets; consumer remapping/dependency cloning.
- Runtime resource/pixel verification, build/serialization/undo/save-reload checks
  for every unverified adapter, and remaining larger/custom-format target work.

Extend `/textures` with typed inspect/settings/platform/import/reimport/mips,
statistics, and validation adapters. Direct source-file rewriting is out of
scope unless the caller explicitly enables import/reimport and provides a
validated source path.

## Capability Matrix Requirements

The capability response must distinguish these states for every family:

- `generic`: list/describe/property/save operations only;
- `inspect`: dedicated read-only adapter;
- `edit`: dedicated typed mutation support;
- `spawn_or_create`: asset or scene-object creation;
- `compile_or_rebuild`: derived-data/graph compilation support;
- `validate`: dedicated compatibility and integrity checks.

The matrix must include at least `world`, `level`, `scene`, `level_sequence`,
`behavior_tree`, `blackboard`, `state_tree`, `environment_query`, `data_asset`,
`primary_data_asset`, `data_registry`, `sound_wave`, `sound_cue`, `metasound`,
`sound_class`, `sound_mix`, `sound_submix`, `texture`, `render_target`,
`texture_array`, `landscape`, `foliage`, and `niagara`. A family must not be
reported as fully implemented merely because generic property serialization
can load its UObject.

The `/assets/capabilities` response now includes these per-family flags and
support levels while preserving its legacy family and operation arrays. A live
contract check covers required families and distinguishes generic-only,
partial, and unavailable adapter states; optional-plugin families use the
current project plugin enabled state. An ordered-batch live check covers
dry-run, mixed success and failure, stop-on-error, legacy compatibility, save,
and disposable-asset cleanup.

## Blueprint graph organization

Implement a deterministic layout service: separate execution and data edges,
collapse cycles into strongly connected components, assign topological layers,
minimize crossings with barycenter ordering, reserve event/root/result lanes,
preserve locked nodes, resolve overlaps, and return moved/skipped/unresolved
statistics. Support dry-run, direction, spacing, scope, and locked-node options.

## Native integration

Use public UE 5.7 APIs first. Add editor dependencies only when required:
PhysicsAssetEditor, Persona, AnimationBlueprintEditor, ControlRig,
ControlRigDeveloper, ControlRigEditor, RigVM, RigVMDeveloper, RigVMEditor,
MaterialEditor, and TextureEditor. Keep private-header usage isolated in
version-specific adapters. The project-level `VisualStudioTools` plugin entry was
removed because the installed optional IDE integration produced an invalid
cached module-rules assembly; the editor/MCP target now builds authoritatively.

- Run Python syntax and wrapper serialization tests.
- Test route registration, capability discovery, invalid classes, dry-run, and errors.
- For each asset family: inspect, mutate, validate bad input, check dirty state,

- Verify material and animation compilation, Blend Space triangulation, Physics
  Asset references, Control Rig/RigVM compilation, Modular Rig connector
  resolution, and graph-layout overlap results.
- Verify `/editor/status` during editor idle, PIE, paused PIE, and no-game-world states.
- Verify viewport get/set, actor list/search/spawn/select/duplicate, confirmation-protected delete, and asset-editor open/focus/status/close in an editor session.
- Verify class search, parent filtering, Blueprint-only filtering, class

  Engine and project classes.

## Recommended UE5 Editor Productivity Tools

The asset-family adapters above should be complemented by the following
editor-workflow tools. They are prioritized by how often they remove manual
work during normal level and gameplay iteration.

### 1. Map Lifecycle and Safety

Complete `/worlds/list`, `/worlds/create`, `/worlds/load`, `/worlds/save`, and
`/worlds/validate`. Before a load, report all dirty packages and require an
explicit confirmation when changing maps would discard unsaved work. Return
the loaded world path, map name, affected packages, and resulting editor
state.

#### Goal and current baseline

The feature gives an MCP client deterministic control over the editor's map
lifecycle without using unrestricted console commands or interactive editor
dialogs. The current baseline includes `/world/inspect`, `/world/save`, and the
new `/worlds/load` route plus the `load_editor_world` Python tool. The load
route already validates the package path, verifies that the `.umap` exists,
rejects map changes during PIE, reports dirty packages through an HTTP 409,
requires `bConfirm=true` before risking unsaved changes, and returns the loaded
world state.

Remaining work covers discovery, creation, validation, save-policy choices,
consistent plural route names, structured response DTOs, and automated editor
integration tests.

#### In scope

- List project and plugin map assets with directory, recursive, search, and
  pagination filters.
- Inspect a specified map without making it the active editor world where the
  public asset APIs allow this safely.
- Create a blank map or create one from a template map.
- Load an existing map with explicit dirty-package policy.
- Save the current map, or save it under a new `/Game` package path.
- Validate package naming, asset type, file existence, external actor state,
  world settings, streaming/sublevel references, and missing dependencies.
- Return the same world-status shape after create, load, and save operations.
- Expose one Python MCP wrapper per native route with LLM-oriented parameter
  descriptions and explicit confirmation semantics.

The first delivery does not include World Partition cell control, Data Layer
mutation, sublevel management, Level Instances, landscape/foliage authoring,
or arbitrary editor commands. Those remain separate route families so map
lifecycle operations stay small and auditable.

#### Route and tool contract

| MCP tool | Native route | Method | Request | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `list_editor_worlds` | `/worlds/list` | GET | `directory_path`, `recursive`, `search`, `limit`, `offset` | Stable array of package path, object path, name, mount point, and file status |
| `inspect_editor_world` | `/worlds/inspect` | GET | Optional `world_path`; empty means current world | World identity, active/dirty flags, actor count, world type, settings class, partition and streaming summary |
| `inspect_editor_world_settings` | `/worlds/settings` | GET | Active persistent editor world | Typed values, numeric bounds and native enum choices |
| `set_editor_world_settings` | `/worlds/settings` | PATCH | Optional `world_path` guard; numeric/bool/class/enum settings; dry-run and save | Current typed values and changed/dirty/saved state |
| `create_editor_world` | `/worlds/create` | POST | `world_path`, optional `template_path`, `save`, `confirm` | Created world state and changed/saved packages |
| `load_editor_world` | `/worlds/load` | POST | `world_path`, `dirty_policy`, `confirm` | Loaded world state, previous world, and dirty/affected packages |
| `save_editor_world` | `/worlds/save` | POST | Optional `world_path`, `save_as`, `confirm` | Saved world state and saved/failed packages |
| `validate_editor_world` | `/worlds/validate` | POST | `world_path`, `load_dependencies`, `run_map_check` | `valid`, errors, warnings, missing references, and map-check findings |

Use snake_case in Python and the existing reflected PascalCase native DTO
fields on the REST boundary. During migration, retain `/world/inspect` and
`/world/save` as compatibility aliases; document `/worlds/*` as canonical and
remove aliases only in a future major version.

Extend `FWorldOperationReq` rather than reusing actor or generic asset DTOs:

- `WorldPath`: target package or object path.
- `TemplatePath`: optional source map for creation.
- `DirtyPolicy`: `fail`, `save`, or `discard`; default `fail`.
- `bSave`: persist a newly created or modified map.
- `bSaveAs`: save the current map at `WorldPath`.
- `bConfirm`: required for discard, overwrite, and save-as replacement.
- `bLoadDependencies`: include dependency checks during validation.
- `bRunMapCheck`: include editor Map Check diagnostics.

Add a structured `FWorldOperationResponse` with `Success`, `Operation`,
`PreviousWorldPath`, `WorldPath`, `PackagePath`, `MapName`, `bDirty`,
`bSaved`, `DirtyPackages`, `ChangedPackages`, `SavedPackages`, `Warnings`, and
`Errors`. List and validation routes may use dedicated response DTOs but must
reuse the same world identity fields.

#### Safety and state-transition rules

1. Normalize object paths to long package names and reject paths outside
   mounted Unreal content roots before any mutation.
2. Resolve the target through Asset Registry and filesystem checks and verify
   it is a `UWorld`/map package. Do not call `LoadMap` for an invalid target.
3. Reject create/load/save-as while PIE, SIE, a modal operation, map load, or
   another world mutation is active. Read-only list/inspect may continue.
4. Gather dirty world, external actor, and content packages before a map
   transition. Return them in a structured 409 response when policy is `fail`.
5. `dirty_policy=save` saves the reported packages and aborts the load if any
   save fails. It must never silently fall back to discard.
6. `dirty_policy=discard` requires `bConfirm=true`; confirmation applies only
   to the exact request and must not become server session state.
7. Creating or saving over an existing map requires `bConfirm=true` and must
   report the existing target before replacement.
8. After mutation, reacquire the editor world rather than retaining pointers
   from before `LoadMap`, then serialize the actual resulting editor state.
9. If validation or preflight fails, preserve the active world, selection,
   viewport, and dirty state. If the UE load itself fails, return a failure and
   the currently active world identity instead of claiming the target loaded.
10. Run all editor mutations on the game thread and serialize world-changing
    requests so two MCP calls cannot race through map transitions.

#### Delivery steps

**Phase M1 — Harden the implemented load slice (implemented)**

- [x] Add `DirtyPolicy` to `FWorldOperationReq`, retaining `bConfirm` compatibility.
- [x] Split dirty map packages from dirty content packages in the response.
- [x] Validate the resolved asset class through Asset Registry in addition to the
  `.umap` filename check.
- [x] Return `FWorldOperationResponse` for success and a structured conflict body
  for preflight failures.
- [x] Add an in-process world-mutation guard and game-thread assertion.
- [x] Update `load_editor_world` to expose `dirty_policy` and parse no state locally.

**Phase M2 — Canonical inspect, list, and validate (implemented)**

- [x] Add `/worlds/inspect` and `/worlds/save`, keeping singular aliases.
- [x] Implement `/worlds/list` with Asset Registry filters and deterministic sort
  by package path; apply `offset` and `limit` after filtering.
- [x] Implement fast validation without opening the map. Add optional dependency
  checks, and run Map Check only when the target is active or can be inspected
  without an unsafe transition.
- [x] Add MCP wrappers and document behavior for clean, dirty, missing, and invalid
  map cases.

**Phase M3 — Create, template, save-as, and save policy (implemented)**

- [x] Implement blank-map creation with `UEditorLoadingAndSavingUtils`.
- [x] Implement template creation only after validating the template as a map.
- [x] Add explicit save and save-as behavior, overwrite confirmation, package
  dirtying, Asset Registry notification, and post-save existence verification.
- [x] Implement `dirty_policy=save` using a non-interactive package-save path and
  return individual failures without continuing to load.

**Phase M4 — Reliability and compatibility**

- Add request/response contract tests for every DTO field and casing rule.
- Add editor automation coverage for state transitions and failure recovery.
- Verify World Partition/external-actor maps without adding partition mutation.
- Exercise project maps, plugin maps, unsaved new maps, redirected maps, and
  source-control read-only files.
- Mark the feature complete only after README status, route inventory, Python
  tool schemas, and implementation-plan status all agree.

#### Test matrix

| Case | Setup/action | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| Clean load | Load valid map while editor is idle and clean | 200; requested map becomes active and response paths match editor status |
| Package-form path | Load `/Game/Maps/TestMap` | Same result as a valid object path |
| Object-form path | Load `/Game/Maps/TestMap.TestMap` | Normalized and loaded successfully |
| Missing map | Load nonexistent package | 400 validation error; active world unchanged |
| Wrong asset type | Supply a non-world asset | 400 type error; no load attempted |
| Dirty fail policy | Dirty map/content then load with default policy | 409 with sorted dirty package lists; active world and dirty flags unchanged |
| Dirty save policy | Load with `dirty_policy=save` | All dirty packages save before load; any save failure aborts transition |
| Dirty discard policy | Load with discard but no confirmation | 409; retry instruction and affected packages returned |
| Confirmed discard | Load with discard and confirmation | Target loads; response records packages dirty before transition |
| PIE/SIE active | Attempt create/load/save-as during play | 409; play session and active map remain unchanged |
| Duplicate create | Create at existing path without confirmation | 409; existing map unchanged |
| Template create | Create from valid template | New independent map has requested path and can save/reopen |
| Save current | Dirty active map then save | Dirty flag clears and package timestamp/registry state updates |
| Save-as | Save active map to a new path | New map becomes active; original remains intact |
| Concurrent mutation | Send two world mutations together | One executes; the other returns conflict/busy without racing |
| Load failure recovery | Force unreadable/corrupt target | Failure includes actual current world; editor remains usable |

#### Definition of done

- All six canonical route contracts and Python tools are implemented and listed
  by MCP discovery with accurate required/optional fields.
- No map-changing path uses console commands, dialogs, or implicit confirmation.
- Every destructive or data-loss-capable path has an explicit preflight and
  request-scoped confirmation.
- Clean, dirty-save, dirty-discard, PIE rejection, invalid target, create,
  template, save, save-as, and recovery tests pass in UE 5.7.
- Existing `/world/inspect`, `/world/save`, editor actor, viewport, PIE, undo,
  and asset routes continue to pass regression tests.
- README examples, implementation status, and the test plan match the shipped
  behavior and clearly label World Partition/Data Layer/sublevel mutation as
  future work.

Extend the existing `/editor/play` controls with `/editor/logs`,

Support filtered Output Log retrieval, Automation Test discovery/execution and
results, Map Check diagnostics, and deterministic editor or PIE screenshots.
Runtime inspection must distinguish the editor world from the PIE game world.

Status: implemented for bounded project-log retrieval, active-world Map Check,

and sanitized PNG screenshot request/status. Log and screenshot responses label

Add `/scene/actors/query`, `/scene/actors/components`, and

Status: implemented for placed actors. Component mutations use editor

### 4. World Partition, Data Layers, Sublevels, and Level Instances

Add `/worlds/partition`, `/worlds/data-layers`, `/levels/sublevels`, and
`/levels/visibility`. Support inspection plus explicit loading, unloading,
activation, visibility, and add/remove operations for public UE editor APIs.
Report affected actors and dirty packages for every mutation.

Status: implemented for current-world partition/external-actor inspection,
Data Layer state and visibility control, and streaming sublevel listing,
transformed addition, confirmation-protected removal, and visibility. Mutations
dirty the owning world package and use public editor subsystem/level utilities.

Initial Level Instance routes now inspect current-world instances and loaded
actors, create native standalone instances from saved maps, edit transforms,
replace source maps, load/unload, validate references, and remove instances.
`/levels/instances`, `/validate`, `/create`, and `/operation` use public native
interfaces/subsystem APIs. Structural edits use transactions and explicit
save; unload, replacement, and removal require confirmation, preserve dirty
loaded content, and reject active editing contexts. Map-reference validation
uses native ancestor checks and a bounded 128-map source traversal to reject
direct and indirect cycles. `wait=true` drains native unload requests before
reporting completion. Loading state is transient editor state and is not saved
as an initially-unloaded policy. A three-map live fixture passed creation,
loaded-actor transforms, unload/reload, replacement, validation, and cycle
guards. A fresh editor session verified the saved GUID, source map, transform,
and loaded actor position; confirmed removal remained removed after map reload.
Source-edit sessions now use `enter_edit`, `commit`, and `discard` operations.
Inspection includes editing state, source dirty packages, loaded/editing actors,
and native edit/commit/discard eligibility. Dirty commit requires explicit save;
discard requires confirmation. Commit saves the identified source packages
through UE's automation-safe API before native commit/refresh, and preserves the
editing session when saving fails or unresolved packages remain. Ordinary
lifecycle operations remain blocked during an active editing context.
A two-instance fixture passed edit preview, dirty-commit rejection without save,
source save/commit, refresh of both instances, confirmed discard with unchanged
source bytes, and clean exit without saving. A fresh editor session verified the
committed source coordinates and both instances; the discarded position was
absent.
Confirmed `break` now delegates actor copying/removal to the native subsystem.
Dry runs report source actors and affected owning packages; requests support
depth 1–8, a 512-actor traversal bound, folder preservation, and explicit save.
The response reports that native break clears undo history and is not atomic or
undoable. Surviving copies are reconciled with the owning level, and mismatched
counts/classes or native failures return partial-result errors without saving.
Active editing, dirty source content, invalid/cyclic source maps, authored Level
Scripts, and World Partition/external-actor source or destination packages are
rejected before copying. A nested-map live fixture passed recursive break,
confirmation/depth/wait guards, composed world positions, preserved folders,
active-edit rejection, owning-map save, undo reset, and unchanged source-map
hashes. A fresh editor verified saved ordinary actors, positions, and folder
paths. Unloaded shallow break retained the nested instance; unloaded recursive
break flattened it. Both passed with folder preservation disabled, and unsaved
operations reported the dirty owning map. The fixture exposed and fixed editor
queries resetting an omitted limit to one row; omitted limits now preserve
their documented defaults. Test maps were removed afterward.
Packing, property overrides, complex moved-package commits, and World
Partition/external actor persistence remain open.

### 7. Sequencer Authoring

Extend the implemented Level Sequence inspection routes with typed
`/level-sequences/bindings`, `/level-sequences/tracks`,
`/level-sequences/sections`, `/level-sequences/keys`, and
`/cinematic/camera-cuts` mutations. Cover common transform, visibility,
property, skeletal-animation, audio, camera-cut, fade, and shot workflows;
use preview and confirmation before deleting bindings, tracks, or sections.

Status: in progress. Possessable binding removal and allowlisted transform,
visibility, float-property, fade, audio, and skeletal-animation track/section
add/remove routes now expose
dry-run previews, affected-section counts, explicit confirmation for removal,
transactional edits, and optional save. Track and section lists return indices
within each binding or the master-track scope. Float, transform, visibility,
audio, and skeletal-animation channels support key inspection, set, and
confirmed removal. Audio sections require a Sound asset; skeletal-animation
sections require an animation and a compatible target Skeletal Mesh for
skeleton validation. The `set_animation` section operation edits play rate,
reverse, slot name, notifier/custom-mode flags, and first-loop/start/end offsets;
section readback reports these settings, offset edits reject values that exceed
the source clip, and fixed play-rate edits adjust the section duration to
preserve its animation span. Edits support dry-run, transactional changes,
dirty tracking, and optional save. The `set_audio` operation edits start offset,
looping, subtitle suppression, attenuation override, and attenuation settings;
it bounds start offset against the finite sound duration and exposes those
values in section readback. `/cinematic/shots` now lists, adds, renames, and
confirmation-removes named shots; shot and subsequence creation reject
recursive nesting. Possessables can bind a placed actor in the current editor
world through `actor_path`, and binding inspection resolves its object path.
Spawnable bindings can copy a placed actor into a sequence-owned template or
create a class-only template from an actor class's defaults; class-only creation
requires `class_path` and `name`. Binding inspection reports binding type and
template class. The canonical
`/cinematic/camera-cuts` route validates camera bindings and nonoverlapping
frame ranges, with dry-run previews and confirmed removal. `/cinematic/cameras`
creates placed CineCameraActors and inspects/edits placed or sequence-template
cameras through public lens, filmback, and focus setters. `/level-sequences/evaluate`
plays from the transform section start through a requested frame, advancing
the sequence player in a disposable preview world for at most 600 display
frames. Preview mode plays a native actor possessable with its transform track
and optional visibility and top-level float-property tracks. It returns the
sampled transform, hidden state, and float property value. It rejects other
bindings, master tracks, spawnables, non-native classes, duplicate supported
tracks, and other track types. When `actor_path` is supplied, it verifies the
current possessable resolves to that placed actor and seeds the preview proxy
from its transform. Set `bPlayOnEditorActor` to opt into advancing that exact
bound actor in the current editor world. Direct mode supports the same transform,
visibility, and float-property combination and restores those actor values and
the map package's prior dirty state before responding. It expands only the
transient sequence copy's playback range when needed. Other track combinations,
specialized audio and animation controls beyond these section settings, camera
animation/layout, and take authoring remain open.
