validation, confirmation, removal, and disposable-asset cleanup across
transform, visibility, float-property, fade, audio, and skeletal-animation
tracks, including skeletal-section settings dry-run, invalid-rate rejection,
readback, and audio-section setting edits, plus shot creation, naming, removal,
reverse-nesting rejection, and
placed-actor binding resolution. The live smoke test now advances the sequence
player through the requested time, evaluates transform, visibility, and float
property together on a class-only proxy, and samples the same combination on a
placed-actor binding in preview and direct modes. Direct mode confirms it
restores the placed actor's transform, visibility, float property, and map dirty
state. Other track combinations are not covered. A two-session smoke test saves
a sequence with a placed-actor binding, transform key, actor-based and
class-only spawnable camera templates, and camera cut; it restarts the editor,
verifies them from the saved asset, and removes the disposable file. The
two-session smoke also saves a configured skeletal-animation section and checks
its adjusted range, play rate, reverse, slot, notifier, custom-mode, and offset
settings after restart, and audio-section looping, subtitle, attenuation
override, and attenuation asset-reference settings. The same
restart test verifies saved focal length, manual focus distance, and filmback
on a CineCamera template after the source editor actor is deleted. Full scene
playback is not yet tested.

### Console-Command Safety Boundary

Do not add a general unrestricted console-command endpoint. If diagnostics
need console access, expose a separate explicitly allowlisted route for safe
read-only commands and approved console variables. Reject commands that can
load maps, execute arbitrary scripts, alter project configuration, or perform
unbounded mutations.

## Broader UE5 Editor Coverage Audit

The plugin does not yet cover every normal UE5 editor workflow. The following
matrix records the remaining tool families needed for broad editor coverage;
each future family must use the common dry-run, dirty-state, save, validation,
and destructive-confirmation contract.

| Editor domain | Current coverage | Missing high-value tools |
|---|---|---|
| Content Browser and asset pipeline | Generic list, properties, save, duplicate, rename, delete, referencers; texture, native audio Sound Wave, and OBJ/glTF/GLB Static Mesh source import/reimport and diagnostics; Content Browser selection/reveal | Other source formats and asset families, migrate, consolidate, collections, broader redirector workflows |
| World building | Map lifecycle; actor/component editing; Data Layers/sublevels; native Level Instance lifecycle, source editing, and confirmed break in ordinary maps; typed persistent World Settings physics, class overrides, rendering, Lightmass and per-map navigation configuration/native system lifecycle; ordinary-map native navigation bounds/build and bounded projection/path queries; direct-native-parent filter Blueprint costs/exclusions/flags and native box modifier painting/replacement and direct-native-parent NavArea Blueprint definitions and native simple off-mesh links | Remaining World Settings families, World Partition cells, Level Instance packing/overrides and external-actor persistence, landscape, foliage, splines, volumes, lighting, reflection captures, post-process |
| Geometry and procedural content | Static/Skeletal Mesh settings plus guarded Static Mesh OBJ/glTF/GLB import/reimport | PCG graphs/components, Geometry Script workflows, Modeling Tools, Nanite diagnostics, collision generation, FBX and Skeletal Mesh import/reimport |
| Materials and textures | Material graph and partial typed settings; texture settings/rebuild | Material Functions, Material Layers, parameter collections, shader/statistics diagnostics, texture source/mips/import/reimport, render targets, virtual textures |
| Animation, rigs, and physics | Animation assets/Blueprint inspection; Physics Asset body/shape/constraint/collision/profile/drive editing including convex-hull topology replacement, per-body runtime collision-mesh checks, body/constraint initialization, bounded simulation through 600 frames, per-frame stability sampling, and impulse-response diagnostics; typed Control Rig hierarchy, values, limits, settings, spaces, RigVM graph authoring, dynamic array-pin CRUD, nested pin inspection, and structural validation with optional VM compile; nested Modular Rig overrides and structural dependency reporting | Broader RigVM node families, IK Retargeter, Pose Search, Motion Matching, skeletal sockets and virtual bones |
| VFX | Niagara utilities present (see NiagaraUtils sections) | Niagara systems, emitters, modules, parameters, simulations, renderers, and validation |
| Audio | Typed Sound Wave settings/validation/rebuild; typed Sound Class/Mix/Submix settings and hierarchy/adjuster/effect-chain authoring; Sound Cue and MetaSound graph authoring/compile/validation; typed attenuation controls/curves/routing/native volume evaluation, plugin settings and concurrency creation; native audio import/reimport; Dialogue Voice/Wave creation/settings/contexts/native resolution/validation; Quartz PIE runtime clocks, dynamic time signatures/pulse overrides, quantized control commands, cancellation, metronome/callback polling and quantized SoundBase playback/spatial attachment/control; persistent SCS/inherited/native default-subobject and placed-instance Audio Component settings; modulation parameter/bus/mix/patch/generator and Audio Bus creation, settings, stages/inputs, conversion/sampling and validation; file-driven patch import/reimport and native runtime curve baking; native modulation PIE destinations/values/mix/global/filter/batch/device-wide controls, live envelope-follower recordings with Audio Bus sends, native audio-thread logical-sound snapshots, guarded profiles and bounded native Unreal Insights trace capture | Advanced Audio Component properties; plugin-specific typed parameters; hardware-voice summaries and CPU/DSP trace analysis |
| UI | Widget-tree CRUD and reflected properties | Widget layout/design-time tooling, bindings, animations, named slots, styles/themes, CommonUI stacks/actions, input routing validation |
| Gameplay and AI | Blueprints, Enhanced Input, native Behavior Tree/Blackboard and EQS graph authoring plus live PIE controls; owned native PIE character/controller movement probes with move completion and lifecycle controls | broader StateTree parameters/bindings/schema coverage and live controls, broader EQS providers/runtime coverage, AI Perception, Gameplay Ability System, Gameplay Tags, Game Feature plugins, Smart Objects, Mass Entity tooling |
| Cinematics | Level Sequence metadata/settings plus possessable and class/actor-template spawnable bindings, initial typed tracks/sections/keys, bounded preview and restored-editor-actor playback for transform plus visibility and float-property tracks, guarded camera cuts, shots, subsequences, and CineCamera creation/lens/focus settings | Other track combinations, specialized tracks/channels, camera animation/layout, Take Recorder |
| Debugging and quality | PIE lifecycle, global undo/redo, reflection discovery | Output Log, breakpoints, Blueprint debugger, Map Check, Automation Tests, screenshots, runtime actor inspection, network emulation, replay controls |
| Build and delivery | Editor target build verification outside the plugin API | C++ compile/build status, cook/package/launch, shader/derived-data status, device deployment, crash-report collection |
| Collaboration | Source-control provider/status/history and guarded operations for project assets/files, including Git missing-file restore and deletion submission | Checkout-enabled provider verification, changelists, general revision download/diff/sync, multi-user session state |
| Editor extensibility | HTTP routes and Python MCP wrapper; Editor Utility discovery/spawn/run (unverified); Remote Control Presets (list, inspect, create, expose/unexpose properties and functions, value set; `/remote-control/presets*`, verified by smoke_remote_control_live.py) | Editor Utility Widgets/Blueprints, controlled Python execution, command/menu registration inspection |

### World Settings Progress

`GET /worlds/settings` inspects the active persistent editor world's supported
native World Settings fields, numeric bounds/integer requirements and enum choices.
`PATCH /worlds/settings` edits world gravity override, Kill Z/world bounds, VR
world scale, client-side streaming-volume policy, precomputed visibility,
distance-field rendering settings and packed lightmap size. Nested Lightmass
controls cover bounce counts, quality/smoothness, lighting scale, environment and
diffuse intensity, volume sampling/brick memory, ambient occlusion and debug flags.
Typed native enum values select visibility aggressiveness and volume lighting
method. Class overrides cover GameMode, Kill Z damage, default physics volume and
collision handler, with native subclass/concrete-class and NoClear validation.

The complete request is validated before changing any field; unsupported names,
nonfinite/out-of-range values, fractional integers, non-power-of-two lightmap
sizes, hidden enums and incompatible class references are rejected. Optional
WorldPath is an exact persistent-map package guard. Inspection exposes
`forced_bool_settings`: World Partition forces `bPrecomputeVisibility=false`.
Attempts to enable it reject the entire request before any scalar or other field
changes, matching native ApplyWorldPartitionForcedSettings on load. A partitioned
fixture passed mixed-request rejection and the settings/undo/save/PIE regression,
followed by cold restart persistence and cleanup.
Mutations require PIE and
simulation to stop, use a native editor transaction and property notifications,
and preserve clean no-ops. Dry-run returns current values and a proposed changed
flag without mutation. Optional save requires an existing /Game map and saves
the entire map, including prior unsaved edits. Lighting edits require a separate
lighting build; class overrides take effect when starting gameplay.

Ordinary and World Partition native fixtures passed mixed numeric/bool/enum/class
edits, atomic rejection, dry-run, undo/redo, no-op, class clearing, save and PIE
guards. Both fixtures passed a cold editor restart with all supported settings
unchanged and clean packages. Native physics/runtime behavior and lighting build
results are not inferred from these persistence tests. HLOD, world
composition/origin policies, Nanite, audio-zone and other nested World Settings
adapters remain pending. Navigation configuration support is described below.

The same route now inspects stored/effective navigation configuration separately,
reports native live-system identity and override state, and accepts typed
`Navigation` edits when `bSetNavigation=true`. Supported config classes are the
generic native config, native Null config, and this plugin's
`PersistentNavigationSystemConfig` subclass of `UNavigationSystemModuleConfig`.
The latter retains native creation/configuration behavior and saves all config
fields rather than relying on delta defaults. A cold restart exposed UE 5.7's
module-config PostInitProperties copying project defaults into delta-omitted false
flags; the subclass's persistent-save serialization prevents that loss. Maps
using this subclass require UE5_MCP and NavigationSystem to remain available.

Controls cover a compatible concrete navigation-system class, unique supported
agent indices 0-15 (an explicit empty subset is valid), default agent name, and
module flags for static navigation, client creation, automatic nav-data spawning
and spawning in the bounds level. Agent selections reference project definitions;
they do not create agent definitions. Select an inspected supported config class
explicitly when converting an existing native module config. Replacing a stored
config or disabling navigation requires confirmation. Active effective overrides
reject stored-config edits instead of changing the override owner's configuration.
Whole-request preflight also protects scalar fields when navigation inputs fail.

Changes duplicate a map-owned config and retain the previous object for undo,
then use the native World Settings property notification to recreate the editor
navigation system. Only World Settings enters the transaction: capturing UWorld
would restore transient navigation pointers on undo and orphan rooted crowd
managers. A live unload test found this lifetime issue and passed after the fix.
Ordinary and World Partition tests passed dry-run/no allocation, malformed mixed
requests/no partial edits, flags/agent masks, map ownership, no-op/no allocation,
native undo/redo, confirmed disable/restore, empty mask, save and PIE guards,
world unloading and cold restart with every stored field retained. The scalar
World Settings transaction/persistence regression also passed. Native recreation
can queue navigation data work; the configuration route alone does not assert a
completed navmesh build or validate pathfinding. Agent-definition and broader
NavMesh settings authoring remain pending.

`/navigation/inspect` reports native editor-world navigation data identities,
agent configuration and rebuild state, loaded bounds geometry, locks and native
running/remaining build task counts. Bounds/data rows are capped at 256 with
full counts and truncation flags. `/navigation/bounds` creates, updates and
confirmed-deletes native box `ANavMeshBoundsVolume` actors in the persistent
level of ordinary maps. Geometry uses UE's CubeBuilder/volume brush factory,
not an actor-only placeholder. Updates define full half extents/location and
axis-aligned unit-scale geometry, use native transactions for actor and brush
component references, and notify navigation. Dry-run and clean no-op are supported.

`/navigation/build` adapts UE's blocking native current-world build. It requires
confirmation, eligible bounds, no running generation tasks, and no blocking
native build lock; the automatic-editor-update lock is ignored just as in UE's
explicit Build implementation. Build preflight supports dry-run. The response
reports elapsed time, native data identities and final task state; idle task
counts alone are not represented as proof of navigability. Optional save saves
the current persistent map, including prior unsaved map edits. Loaded-sublevel
package save coverage remains separate. Bounds/build mutations reject PIE/SIE
and World Partition; dedicated partition navigation-builder workflows remain
pending. The synchronous native build cannot be canceled through the HTTP route
while its game-thread call is executing.

`/navigation/query` runs native point projection or synchronous pathfinding on
registered current-editor-world data, with optional explicit data/filter selection.
It never creates missing navigation data. A copied query filter bounds path search
to 16-65536 nodes without mutating the cached native filter. Projection extents,
coordinates, path cost and returned rows are bounded. Results distinguish failed
endpoint projection, native success/result, partial path and search-limit state,
and return native cost/length and full point count even when rows are truncated.
This is an editor-world query, not a selected-PIE-world query or locomotion test.

A native floor/wall fixture passed brush bounds CRUD, geometry undo/redo,
dry-run/no-op and malformed-input/confirmation guards, native builds, projection
onto the generated floor, paths detouring around a blocking wall, partial-path
allow/refuse behavior across disconnected surfaces, query limits/truncation,
and a shorter direct path after wall removal/rebuild. Saved bounds and generated
navmesh paths survived a cold editor restart and another native rebuild. Fixture
map unload/delete passed. Broader collision/area and smart-link authoring, custom/inherited
filter adapters, additional agents, PIE queries and partition navigation builds
remain open.

`GET/POST /navigation/filters` inspects, creates and updates `/Game` Blueprints
whose direct native parent is `UNavigationQueryFilter`. The adapter edits only
the selected Blueprint-owned generated-class defaults, compiles through the native
Blueprint editor APIs, and optionally saves the asset. Whole-request preflight
validates up to 64 unique concrete compatible NavArea classes, finite travel costs
in [1,1e6], entering costs in [0,1e6], and 16-bit include/exclude masks. Explicit
area-list replacement supports clearing; omitted lists and -1 masks preserve
current defaults. Dry-run and clean no-op preserve the asset/package state.
Inspection reports structural/compile diagnostics and the generated class path
usable by `/navigation/query`. Mutation rejects PIE/SIE; read-only inspection
works during PIE through loaded objects/Asset Registry rather than editor scripting
existence checks. Missing reads do not create failed-load packages or block later
creation. Native/shared class defaults and unrelated filters are never edited.

Native `UNavigationQueryFilter::PostEditChangeProperty` invalidates cached filters
across navigation systems. UObject's native undo path reissues the notification,
so editor undo/redo also updates actual query behavior. A generated-navmesh fixture
passed travel-cost changes without changing path length, exclusion of the default
area, include/exclude mask rejection of paths, clearing overrides, immediate cached
query updates, undo/redo, unchanged default-filter query costs, preflight/no partial
edits, dry-run, no-op, asset save and PIE read/edit guards. A cold restart preserved
all settings, including entering-cost settings, and reproduced the actual filtered
path cost. The modifier fixture below additionally verifies costs at distinct area
boundaries. Custom/inherited filter classes remain pending. Navigation and navigation-query-filter
capability entries passed availability/operation and unique-JSON-key checks.

`/navigation/query` operation `inspect_filter` reports native registered area IDs
and the selected data's effective cached filter travel/entering costs, include/
exclude masks and native search-node limit before per-query overrides. It runs no
path search and does not change cached filters. Cost-table capacity must be 1-256;
area rows are capped at 256 with counts/truncation and invalid/nonfinite cost slots
reported explicitly. Editor and selected-PIE resolution share the query route's
world/data guards. The MCP tool is `inspect_navigation_filter_costs`.
Native tests compared default-area cost 1 with authored costs 2/5/3, undo restoration
to 2 and entering-cost readback 321 alongside actual path behavior. The fixture
Recast default include mask was 32767, while its Blueprint filter mask was 65535;
the adapter preserves that distinction. Costs alone are not a passability verdict.

`/navigation/modifiers` now creates, updates and confirmed-deletes axis-aligned
native `ANavModifierVolume` box brushes in ordinary persistent editor levels.
The route shares the tested bounds-volume brush/transaction implementation,
validates the full request before editing, supports dry-run/clean no-op, and
reports up to 256 modifier rows with full count/truncation through navigation
inspection. Area assignment and optional source-area replacement use native
setters and navigation-data notification. Complete update references make empty
AreaClass disable painting and empty AreaClassToReplace clear replacement scope.
Native class compatibility is checked before shape changes. Optional save saves
the current persistent map; PIE/SIE and partition volume mutations are rejected.
Experimental resolution and fill-underneath controls, arbitrary volume shapes,
custom/inherited area-base adapters and partition external-actor persistence remain open.

A real floor fixture passed painting a high-cost region, a travel-cost override
choosing a shorter route through it, and a fixed entering cost choosing a detour
without changing the travel-cost override. It also passed nonmatching source-area
replacement leaving the floor unpainted, disabled painting, Null-area blocking
and partial paths, malformed mixed shape/class requests/no partial mutation,
dry-run/no-op, brush/area undo and rebuild, confirmed delete/dry-run/undo, and save.
Modifier geometry/area references, the generated painted navmesh and actual native
default/filtered query behavior survived a cold editor restart. The bounds/build
regression passed alongside the modifier workflow, and owned fixtures unloaded
and deleted cleanly.

`GET/POST /navigation/areas` now inspects, creates and updates `/Game` Blueprints
whose direct native parent is `UNavArea`. Supported fields are finite default
travel/fixed entering costs in [0,1e6], RGBA display color and explicit supported
agent indices 0-15. Omitted/-1 cost values preserve defaults, empty color preserves,
and an explicitly set empty agent list disables all agents. Native area flags are
reported read-only. The selected Blueprint must own its generated class; native
shared defaults are read for creation preflight and never edited. Updates validate
the complete request, use native transactions, compile the Blueprint, and optionally
save the asset. Read-only inspection works during PIE; mutations reject PIE/SIE.
Dry-run and clean no-op preserve defaults/package state.

Area changes use native navigation area unregister/register APIs to refresh live
systems and modifier notifications. A weak per-Blueprint snapshot lets the native
post-undo/redo hook refresh only areas whose supported defaults/class changed;
unrelated transactions do not re-register unchanged areas. Deleted/reparented
Blueprints are dropped from tracking, and the hook is removed on module shutdown.
Inspection reports bounded registration rows with the native area ID for each
current editor-world navigation data object, rather than inferring support from
the requested mask. This is not a completed-generation guarantee: rebuild and
query the actual painted region to verify navigation behavior.

Native tests passed area creation, costs/color/agent edits, native registration and
empty-mask unregistration for the fixture agent, malformed-input/no partial edits,
dry-run, no-op, save, PIE read/edit guards, and native undo/redo refresh. A real
modifier using the new area changed route choice when its default travel or entering
cost changed. A query filter could override that custom area's costs to recover
the shorter crossing route. Cold restart preserved area defaults, native agent
registration, painted navmesh behavior and the filter override. The bounds/build
regression and area capability/unique-JSON-key checks also passed. Additional
native/meta/inherited area bases, custom area flags and agent-definition authoring
remain pending.

`GET/POST /navigation/links` inspects native proxies and creates, updates or
confirmed-deletes plain `ANavLinkProxy` actors with simple point links in ordinary
persistent editor levels. Updates replace up to 64 point links and the full actor
translation/rotation at unit scale. Controls cover actor-local endpoints, native
direction, compatible area class, agent mask, snap radius/height, cheapest-area
snapping and endpoint projection heights. Full preflight precedes any actor/link
change; dry-run, clean no-op, native transactions and optional persistent-map save
are supported. Mutation rejects PIE/SIE, partition maps, derived/custom proxies,
relevant smart links and segment links. Inspection remains bounded to 256 proxies
and 64 point-link rows with counts/truncation, including requested world endpoints
before native projection/snapping.

Point-link property notifications and native actor navigation updates feed the
real navigation octree. `/navigation/query` now reports `mesh_path_flags` and each
mesh path point's native `off_mesh_connection` bit; non-mesh path types are not
decoded as Recast flags. A native Null-area gap fixture had no path before link
creation, then passed left-to-right, right-to-left and bidirectional connections
with actual off-mesh path points. Tests also passed actor-local/world rotation,
empty agent masks, empty-list disabling, area-filter exclusion of the connection,
preflight/no partial mutation, dry-run/no-op, native undo/redo and rebuild, confirmed
delete/dry-run/restore and map save. Proxy settings, generated bidirectional paths
and native area exclusion survived a cold editor restart; the bounds/build
regression and fixture cleanup passed alongside this workflow. Nondefault snapping
and projection-height boundary cases need further fixtures. Smart-link runtime
callbacks/toggling, AI locomotion across links, derived proxies, custom link IDs/
flags, link-definition assets and segment links remain separate pending work.

`/navigation/smart-links` has native smart-only
proxy create/update/delete and selected-PIE `set_enabled` control. Link inspection
and navigation projection/path queries now accept explicit editor/PIE context and
PIE instance selection; cross-world actor/data references are rejected. Editor
configuration uses native component setters and transactions. Runtime toggling
uses the native enabled/disabled-area update without saving editor assets or
replacing movement delegates. The UE target built successfully. Live tests passed
smart-only configuration, preflight/dry-run/no-op, relevance and agent controls,
undo/redo/rebuild, deletion/restore, save, selected-PIE connectivity changes without
explicit rebuilds/running generation tasks, editor-world isolation and two-PIE
state reset. Cold restart also passed persisted proxy/component settings, generated
off-mesh connectivity and clean-package state after native generation settled.
Owned PIE smart-link reached/resume observations and movement probes are
described below; physical-gap locomotion remains pending.

The initial cold-restart check used an immediate combined connectivity/clean-package
assertion and failed. The preserved reproduction passed in a fresh editor with
separate settings, native build-readiness, connectivity and dirty-state checks.
The test waits up to 20 seconds for native generation and the path together; it
does not trigger a rebuild to satisfy the persistence gate. A failure retains its
fixture and writes diagnostic query/navigation/link snapshots. The successful
rerun removed the owned reproduction. Approval-review usage limits temporarily
prevented that launch; normal approval review later succeeded. This gate verifies
the tested ordinary-map fixture, not partition navigation or AI traversal.

`/navigation/query` operations `random_reachable` and `random_navigable`
now adapt the corresponding native navigation queries with selected editor/PIE
world/data/filter context. Radius is bounded to (0,100000], requests to 1-32
attempts, and a copied filter receives the existing bounded search-node setting.
Optional origin projection reports failure without fabricated coordinates. Every
attempt retains native success/failure; successful rows alone contain locations.
The MCP tool is `sample_navigation_points`. Samples are not deterministic or
unique, and native attempts may fail even with valid origin projection. Navigable
samples need not be connected to the origin. Radius follows native navigation
geometry rather than an asserted 3D Euclidean sphere.
A real planar navmesh fixture passed both native operations, independent path
checks for successful points, planar-radius checks, omitted coordinates for failed
attempts, input bounds, failed origin projection and selected-PIE queries. The
bounds/build regression and fixture cleanup passed. A Null-area strip fixture also
verified disconnected regions: reachable samples remained on the origin's island
and passed independent native path queries; native navigable sampling produced
opposite-island points that projected successfully but had no connecting path.
Opposite-island observation uses at most 128 native attempts and fails explicitly
as inconclusive if none is observed; no seed or fabricated point substitutes for
native output. Nonplanar geometry and custom-filter sampling need further fixtures.

### Native PIE Movement Probes

`GET/POST /navigation/agents` creates and controls owned transient native
`ACharacter`/`AAIController` pairs in an explicitly selected PIE world. Creation
projects a feet location onto existing default navigation data and matches capsule
dimensions to its agent config; it never controls or possesses existing user
actors. Native MoveTo, stop, pause and resume operations use path following,
optional filter/partial-path policy and acceptance radius. Inspection reports
actual actor position/velocity, native path status/request, current partial-path
and custom-link-use state, and native completion result/flags with sequence paging.
No movement operation teleports the pawn or edits editor assets.

Wall-clock lifetime is bounded to 0.2-120 seconds, speed to 10-1200 units/second,
retained probes to 16 per PIE world/128 globally, and completion history to 256
events per probe. Expiry destroys owned actors and retains final position/events
until release. Explicit release destroys actors and removes the record; world
cleanup removes matching records, and module shutdown removes ticker/delegate
hooks and releases owned actors. Completion delegates capture weak records and
are detached through their native path-following component even during controller
teardown. Dry-run preflights without actor creation or movement submission.

A real floor/wall fixture passed physical obstacle detours and endpoint arrival,
native success/abort callbacks, pause/resume/stop, exclusive event cursors/pages,
invalid input/filter/dry-run guards, expiry/release, retained-world resource cap,
unchanged editor settings/package state and two-PIE cleanup/reuse. The native
bounds/build regression also passed and fixtures were removed. These probes do not
provide behavior-tree execution, networked agent authority workflows or AI
traversal across physical gaps; those remain pending.

Smart-link probes now accept `watch_link`, `unwatch_link`, and `resume_link`.
`SmartLinkPath` must identify a relevant proxy in the selected PIE world. A
transient UObject listener joins the existing native multicast event without
replacing the proxy's component movement handler or Blueprint callbacks. It
records only its owned pawn, sharing the bounded sequence history with native
move completions; smart-link rows include kind, proxy path and destination.
Repeated watches do not duplicate subscriptions; rejected replacements preserve
the current observer. Dry-run does not bind or resume. Changing the observer while
the pawn uses its watched link is rejected until stop or link resume.

`resume_link` calls the native proxy resume for the owned pawn only when its path
following component currently uses that exact link. Native smart-link reached
events do not automatically pause walking. Separately paused requests still need
ordinary `resume` after custom-link use is cleared. These operations supply no
jump animation or locomotion across a physical gap. Expiry, release, world cleanup
and module shutdown detach the multicast listener and clear its weak callback.

The UE 5.7 target built successfully. The traversal fixture passed reached-event
identity, exactly one event after repeated watch, rejected-watch
preservation, editor-world proxy rejection, dry-run guards, native link resume,
physical walking to the destination, unwatch, release while using a second link,
subscribed-observer teardown on PIE exit, watched-probe expiry and ID reuse in
a fresh PIE session, and unchanged editor proxy/package state. Owned fixtures
were removed. It uses continuous physical floor with
a Null-area navigation strip and a lane clear of the default PIE player spawn.
The initial origin-lane attempt reported native Blocked; separately pausing midway
across the navigation gap and resuming reported native OffPath. Neither result is
rewritten as success; the test and contract use ordinary native link resume while
walking and make no automatic-wait or jump claims.

### Source Control Progress

`/editor/source-control/provider` reports the configured provider, registered
providers, availability, and supported operations. `/status` reports disk and
unsaved-package state plus provider file flags for `/Game` assets and selected
project files, including missing files.
`/operation` adapts checkout, add, revert, and submit with provider eligibility
preflight and dry-run. Revert/submit require confirmation, reject unsaved
packages, and use native package reload and pre-submit validation/finalization
hooks. Revert of loaded worlds/external packages requires unloading first;
provider preferences that delete added files require separate confirmation.
Provider operations are non-atomic, and a failed attempted operation reports
that files may have changed. The UE target builds; a live test with provider
`None` passed status, dry-run, unavailable-provider, and package-path guards.
An isolated content-only project with a local Git repository and no remotes
passed add and submit dry-runs, add, local submit, missing-confirmation and
description rejection, unsaved-package rejection, confirmed revert, native
package reload, and added-file revert confirmation. Git checkout is correctly
reported as unsupported. Successful provider stderr progress is retained as a
warning instead of incorrectly marking the operation failed. Checkout-enabled
provider verification, changelists, and
revision download/diff/sync remain open.

`/editor/source-control/history` now reports bounded pages of native revision
metadata for up to 16 saved assets: revision IDs/numbers, description, submitter,
client, action, date, file size, and branch-source metadata where provided.
Requests accept a 1-50 revision limit and an offset; descriptions are capped at
8192 characters. Counts refer to the history retained by the provider. An
isolated two-commit Git fixture passed metadata comparison against Git, paging,
cached reads, empty pages, and invalid limit/offset rejection. The adapter uses
the native history-update operation rather than treating `UsesFileRevisions`
as a history-availability flag; Git supports history while returning false
for that revision-model flag.

Source-control requests now also accept `FilePaths`: individual project-root
files or files in Content, Config, Source, Plugins, and Build with supported
asset/source/config/text extensions. The resolver rejects outside paths,
generated folders, Git metadata, alternate streams, symlinks, and junctions.
Missing `.uasset`/`.umap` filenames retain package identity and reload behavior;
other project files report no in-memory package dirty state. Git's UE 5.7
missing-file history/revert limitations are handled by fixed read-only Git
metadata/blob commands using the configured binary/repository. This adapter
retains up to 256 revisions, limits metadata output to 16 MiB and blob restore
to 256 MiB, and bounds each read to 30 seconds. Requests cannot choose commands.
An isolated Git fixture passed config-file add/submit/edit/revert, missing text
and texture restoration, package reload, deletion submit/history, and path and
junction guards. Missing maps/external packages and other providers require
separate verification.

### Static Mesh Source Import Progress

`/static-meshes/source` reports LOD geometry counts and source-file status.
`/static-meshes/import` and `/reimport` accept OBJ, glTF, and GLB sources with
dry-run and save controls. OBJ replacement requires explicit confirmation.
glTF scene imports require an unused destination folder, report the actual mesh
path and generated asset list, and use reimport for existing meshes. Generated
OBJ, embedded GLB, and embedded-buffer text glTF fixtures passed live import and
reimport checks. The OBJ fixture also passed replacement and source-path-change
guards. A two-mesh scene with a shared material passed generated-asset reporting,
geometry inspection, occupied-folder rejection, and cleanup. Broader scene
reimport/texture dependency coverage, FBX, and Skeletal Mesh source workflows
remain open.

### Recommended Completion Order

1. Shared contract and capability matrix, then map lifecycle, PIE diagnostics,
   actor components, and Content Browser synchronization.
2. World Partition/Data Layers/Level Instances, content import/reimport, and
   build/validation/source-control tooling.
3. Physics/Control Rig/Modular Rig, Sequencer authoring, PCG, Niagara, and
   advanced animation workflows.
4. MetaSound, CommonUI, StateTree/EQS/GAS, device deployment, and optional
   editor-extensibility integrations.

This order prioritizes deterministic project editing and verification before
specialized authoring systems. Unsupported optional engine plugins must be
reported as unavailable instead of being represented as implemented tools.

## Core game-making loop (2026-11-04)

Verified by `smoke_game_core_live.py`:

- Blueprint class defaults, including inherited fields and native components: `inspect_blueprint_class_defaults`, `set_blueprint_class_default`.
- Project game settings (default map, startup map, GameMode, GameInstance): `inspect_project_game_settings`, `set_project_game_setting`.
- Playtesting a running PIE session: `inspect_play_session`, `send_play_input`.
- Win64 packaging through RunUAT: `package_game`, `get_package_status`, `cancel_package`. Output goes to `Saved/MCPBuilds`.

## create_asset (2026-11-04)

New `POST /assets/create` route (`GameCoreUtils::CreateAsset`) and core-list MCP tool, using engine factories. Kinds: material, material_instance, data_table, curve_float, curve_vector, curve_linear_color, anim_blueprint, blend_space, blend_space_1d, montage, physical_material. Never overwrites; supports dry run and save.

## import_fbx (2026-11-04)

New `POST /assets/import-fbx` route (`GameCoreUtils::ImportFbx`) and core-list MCP tool. Imports FBX as skeletal_mesh, animation or static_mesh using `UFbxFactory` explicitly, which bypasses Interchange and runs synchronously. Reuses a Skeleton on request and reports every asset added to the folder. Never overwrites. Reimport is not implemented.

## Blueprint debugging and C++ feedback (2026-11-05)

- `compile_blueprint` and `compile_editor_blueprints` report errors, warnings and each message with its node. `compile_blueprint` used to report success even when a Blueprint had errors.
- `edit_blueprint_breakpoint`, `list_blueprint_breakpoints`, `inspect_blueprint_debug_state` and `control_blueprint_debugger` set breakpoints and, when one is hit, read the node, call stack, locals and variables, then resume or step. They need a windowed editor; a headless one refuses to add breakpoints.
- While paused, HTTP keeps running and other routes return 409. A pause with no client resumes after `timeout_seconds` and disables that breakpoint.
- `create_cpp_class` adds a class to a project module. `get_live_coding_status` and `compile_cpp_with_live_coding` cover Live Coding, and `get_editor_build_status` now reports `cxx_compile_status`.

## Fixes from building a game with the core tools (2026-11-05)

`tests/build_core_game_live.py` builds and plays Orb Run in `/Game/OrbRun`, using only the core tool list. Building it changed these tools:

- `connect_pins` goes through the graph schema. It now refuses invalid links with the reason, and cast and wildcard pins get their type. Before, cast nodes could not compile.
- `set_pin_default_value` goes through the schema, so class, object and text pins now keep their values. It refuses an object or class that does not exist.
- `control_ue_play_session` `start` plays from the PlayerStart. The old play-from-camera behaviour is now `start_here`.
- `add_widget_to_blueprint` and `remove_widget_from_blueprint` keep the widget variable GUIDs, which stops a compile ensure.
- `set_component_property` tells the component a property changed, as the details panel does, which stops a StaticMesh ensure.

## Standard tool replies and graph editing (2026-11-05)

- Every synchronous tool now passes through one wrapper in `ue5_tools/app.py`. JSON objects carry `success`; failures also carry `errorMessage` and `tool`; empty and `OK` replies become `{"success": true, "tool": ...}`; an unreachable editor or a timeout is a result with advice, not an exception. Lists and plain values such as asset paths are unchanged. Direct HTTP replies are unchanged, apart from the add-node routes below.
- The 13 `add_*_to_graph` routes return `node_id`, `node_title` and `pins`.
- `edit_blueprint_graph` adds nodes, links and pin values in one call, and removes the nodes it added if a step fails. It does not restore links or values changed on nodes already in the graph.
- `read_play_actor_properties` reads live values from an actor in the running game.
- A property-not-found error from the shared property setter suggests similar names, one struct level down, such as `BodyInstance.CollisionProfileName`.

MCP clients now get an object from every synchronous tool: lists and plain values arrive as `{"success": true, "tool": ..., "result": ...}`, and failures carry `errorKind`, `fix` and the `arguments` sent. Create-style tools (`create_`, `add_`, `spawn_`, `duplicate_`, `import_`, `place_`, `insert_`, `copy_`, `upsert_`) also return `id` and `id_source`: `reply` when the editor reported it, `arguments` when it is the name or path requested. `errorKind` is chosen from the message's wording. Python functions called directly keep returning lists and plain values.

`move_play_mouse` points the mouse in the running game at an actor, world location or screen position, and reports what is under it on the Visibility channel. It moves the real system cursor and needs a windowed editor.

## Class search, console and project errors (2026-11-06)

- `list_ue_classes` also finds unloaded Blueprints and filters by parent short name, category, source (`engine_cpp`, `project_cpp`, `blueprint`), module and `can_be_parent`. It now returns an object with `classes`, `total` and `truncated`, and `blueprint_only` is replaced by `source="blueprint"`.
- `execute_console_command` runs one console command with `confirm=True`. It refuses quit, exit, crash, debug, py and python, and logs each command.
- `list_blueprint_errors` compiles the Blueprints under a /Game folder and reports those with errors, without leaving them dirty.
- `get_project_errors` reads this session's log errors, Message Log pages and the last Unreal Build Tool log.
- `get_editor_logs` reads this session's real log file, including under `-abslog`, with exact severity, `category` and `since_line`.

## Graph formatting (2026-11-06)

`organize_blueprint_graph` and `layout_animation_blueprint_graph` use a layered layout in `Core/GraphLayoutUtils.cpp`: break cycles, assign columns with pure nodes beside their users, reduce crossings, then align rows with priority for execution wires. The technique is the one used by [GraphFormatter](https://github.com/howaajin/graphformatter); no code was copied. `organize_blueprint_graph` adds `node_ids` and `dry_run`, and reports crossings and overlaps before and after. Spacing now means the gap between nodes, with new defaults of 100 and 48. Node sizes are estimated.
